docs.title: sticky
docs.text:
Full custom ESP-IDF firmware that turns a Seeed reTerminal Sticky into a tiny.technology device — the e-ink embodiment of tiny, joining phone / web / necklace (Nicla Vision) / voice-necklace (Nicla Voice) as the 5th body, and the most independent one: it has its own Wi-Fi and talks to the backend directly.

Currently shipping fw 0.17.0-m14 over its own OTA channel (sticky-dev) — pinned to the version verified on the glass by a live status receipt (fw_commit 4a1c0d3f, clean, grammar v5). This build ships the pocket lockout — the P-1 safety pillar for a device that lives in fabric next to a microphone: one lock state read at four input choke points, an unlock chord on raw GPIO that the gated layer cannot disable, and a relay that stays answerable because lockout guards the device's inputs, not the owner's reach. Verified live by this site's lane the hour it landed — including the one gate the build missed: a locked device still answers miccheck with room audio (filed P1, documented in Commands until the refusal receipt exists — the pre-registered probe caught exactly what it was written to catch).

Not a mockup: the device's actual framebuffer, fetched over the relay with the screenshot verb — the same ground-truth loop the agent uses to verify its own renders.

docs.title: What it does today
docs.text:
A magnetic 800×480 e-ink card on the fridge that:

  • answers to tiny — polls the relay every 5 s when awake, backing off to 60 s idle; sixteen verbs (render_ui · say · screenshot · page · rotate · tap · swipe · scroll · status · sensors · miccheck · ask · voice · sleep · ota · messages) — fifteen advertised in the heartbeat so the dashboard lights buttons from the device's word, plus swipe (0.16.2), which dispatches but isn't in the caps array yet — the one known advertising gap. All of it reachable from any tiny surface via use_device. Full reference: Commands
  • renders agent-composed cards — text / list / kv / chart / composite / qr / keyboard / menu + a 4-button touch bar; taps flow back as ui_tap events, so the screen is a conversation. Spec: Cards
  • carries the owner's DMs — the messages app lives in firmware: inbox, threads, notification pushes, and replies typed on the e-ink keyboard, fetched with the device's own token — no phone, no owner-side process
  • runs a local shell — stickyOS: home grid, page ring on the UP/DOWN keys, long-press-AI home key, settings, Wi-Fi join with an on-e-ink keyboard, a Bluetooth scan page (NimBLE observer — scan-only, honestly), IMU auto-rotate — stand the device on its side and the UI turns with it (rotate 90 holds, rotate auto releases) — and swipe gestures: vertical scrolls, horizontal turns pages (in logical space, so it survives rotation; a draft outranks a gesture); navigation never touches the network, and every tap path has a relay twin (page …)
  • asks tiny questions — press the AI button, speak: PDM mic → WAV → /api/media → /api/devices/ask → owner-scoped full-agent turn (tools, memory, cross-device reach — it can check another machine's disk from the wall) → answer painted as a card. Same UX as the iOS app, no phone required
  • proves what it shows — screenshot uploads the actual framebuffer (render ground truth); sensors reads I²C live; miccheck measures the room's noise floor; the clock names its own source (sntp/rtc)
  • sleeps like e-ink — deep sleep keeps the goodbye card on glass at 0 mA; the AI button (EXT1) always wakes it
  • updates itself — sha256-pinned OTA, staged, trial-boot with rollback armed

Hardware honesty

  • The Sticky has a PWM buzzer (GPIO48), not a speaker — chimes yes, speech no. Voice input is first-class.
  • E-ink cannot do video: full refresh is physically 1–2 s. Frame sequences are time-lapse cadence, not motion.
  • image/stream card types are planned, not shipped (chart shipped in 0.14.16) — the dashboard refuses what the firmware lacks with the reason rather than pretending.
  • Turkish text is transliterated, not rendered — "Çağatay" shows as "Cagatay" until the extended-glyph font lands. The font has no ç pixels; the docs won't pretend otherwise.

docs.title: The five bodies
docs.text:
graph LR
    T((tiny)) --- P[📱 phone]
    T --- W[🌐 web]
    T --- N[📷 necklace<br/>Nicla Vision]
    T --- V[🎙 voice necklace<br/>Nicla Voice]
    T --- S[🧲 sticky<br/>e-ink, own Wi-Fi]
    style S stroke:#0ff,stroke-width:3px

The necklaces relay through the phone; sticky talks to tiny.technology on its own — heartbeat every 30 s advertising its real capabilities, relay poll every 5 s, direct media upload, self-healing auth that never destroys identity on a single error — three strikes halt polling and raise the rescue portal, keeping the stored token for forensics. See the API contract.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: M10 (stickyOS) in progress; M0–M9 gates closed with on-glass evidence — see the journal. Built end-to-end by tiny (builder + supervisor loops), including the backend route (/api/devices/ask) and this documentation.

docs.title: API CONTRACT — exact wire shapes (source: ~/tinyai-id routes + ~/strands-nicla/firmware)
docs.text: Base URL from config (api, default https://tiny.technology). All device verbs authenticate with deviceId + token IN THE JSON BODY (not headers). Every request: 15 s timeout, TLS. All bodies Content-Type: application/json.

docs.title: Heartbeat — every 30 s (≈60 s when idle, 0.14.14+)
docs.text:
POST /api/devices/heartbeat
{"deviceId":"…","token":"tind_…","capabilities":["render_ui","screenshot","ask","say","sensors","image","stream","sleep","ota","messages"]}
→ 200 {ok:true}
→ 200 {ok:true,"unread":3}   when the beat opts in with "wantUnread":"1" — the DM badge rides the beat, no extra request
→ 401  = revoked/rotated — but never erase identity on ONE 401 (blips happen):
         3 consecutive = auth-halt + rescue portal (0.14.12); do NOT retry-loop

docs.title: Relay poll — every 5 s active · 60 s idle (adaptive, 0.14.14+)
docs.text:
Cadence is adaptive since 0.14.14: 5 s polling while active (an envelope, tap, or boot in the last 2 minutes), stretching to 60 s after two quiet minutes — cutting idle TLS handshakes ~17k→~3.4k/day on the 750 mAh pack. Boot and wake always start ACTIVE (never wake into a 60 s hole), the auth-halted slow path is untouched, and status JSON exposes poll_cadence so the claim is a read, not a belief. Verification note from the bench: the observable for cadence is probe-2 pickup delay, not the field alone — the probe envelope itself is activity, so a single probe always reports a device it just woke up. 

PUT /api/devices/relay
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","max":5}
→ {"messages":[{"id":"env_…","payload":"<SERIALIZED STRING: {\"type\":\"invoke\",\"prompt\":\"…\"}>"}]}  ⚠ payload is a STRING containing JSON (sender JSON.stringify) — parse it, then read .prompt
Execute in order; unknown command → reply help text (never silence).

docs.title: Relay reply — per envelope
docs.text:
PATCH /api/devices/relay
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","inReplyTo":"env_…","payload":"<SERIALIZED JSON STRING ≤8000B>"}
payload string decodes to: {"result":"…"[, "images":[{"url":"https://…","format":"bmp"}]]}
⚠ payload is a string containing JSON, not nested JSON — Nicla's serializer is the reference.

docs.title: Media upload
docs.text:
POST /api/media
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","data":"<base64>","contentType":"image/bmp" | "audio/wav"}
→ {"url":"https://plugin.tiny.technology/…"}   (note: different host than api — matters for OTA host pinning)
b64 of n bytes = 4·⌈n/3⌉; with 8MB PSRAM we buffer whole (≤1MB artifacts) via esp_http_client; chunked-TE streaming is the fallback for bigger.

docs.title: Transcript (durable text)
docs.text:
POST /api/devices/transcript
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","text":"…","label":"sticky-ask","audioUrl":"…","durationS":7}

docs.title: Device event (button taps → owner's activity feed)
docs.text:
POST /api/devices/event
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…", …kind-specific fields}   // kind:"ui_tap", card_id, button_id
(Verify exact field envelope against app/api/devices/event/route.ts during M4 — auth pattern identical to transcript.)

docs.title: OTA channel pointer
docs.text:
PUT /api/firmware/manifest
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","channel":"sticky-stable"}
→ {"bundle":{"url":"https://…manifest.json","sha256":"…"}}
Manifest → files[] each with sha256; hosts must be in the pinned allowlist (tiny.technology, plugin.tiny.technology). Downgrade refusal (0.14.9; the fix for an audited hazard): the original trigger was direction-blind (strcmp difference, not newer) — integrity fully verified, direction unchecked, so a stale pointer would have been installed as faithfully as a fresh one. Since 0.14.9 the device compares versions numerically (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-mN]; unparseable = INCOMPARABLE = refuse, fail closed) and stages only when the pointer is newer — unless the bundle carries force:"1", which installs and logs loudly. force lives as channel state (migration 0035): set at publish time, served in every bundle read, self-clearing on the next forward publish — closing a cross-guard deadlock the audit caught, where the publish rail allowed a forced rollback but dropped the flag the install rail needed to accept it: two guards that individually worked and jointly wedged. The refusal reply is an actionable sentence. The publisher's ancestry check (discipline rule 5) remains in force, the publish route itself now 409s a backwards pointer (force:true = an intentional rollback, spelled out at publish time), and the dashboard's ota action opens a 30-minute watch: fw_before is captured by a fresh probe, every parsed status receipt afterwards feeds the redeem, and the verdict is rendered — ⬆✅ upgraded, ⬆🚨 DOWNGRADED, or ⌛ expired-unredeemed, never silence. Three enforcement points (publish, install, watch), each with its own receipt.

docs.title: /api/devices/ask — shipped in M5, full tools since phase-3 gate #1
docs.text:
POST /api/devices/ask
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","audioUrl":"https://…"} | {"…","text":"what's on my calendar"}
→ {"text":"…", "card":{…render_ui spec…}}       (transcribe when audioUrl, then owner-scoped agent turn)
Design follows transcript/route.ts (device-token auth, no session, off IP limiter, worker resolves owner from token hash). The turn runs the owner's full agent (tools, memory, cross-device reach). Runtime note: this route (and job-run) lives on the Node runtime, not Vercel Edge — Edge's 25 s first-byte deadline on non-streaming responses 504'd every long agent turn; the worker-budget bump alone did not fix it.

docs.title: /api/devices/messages — the DM rail on a device token (option B, 2026-08-26)
docs.text:
POST /api/devices/messages
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","op":"unread"}                    → {"unread":0,"from":[]}
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","op":"inbox"}                     → owner's threads + unread counts
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","op":"thread","with":"<login>"}   → one conversation (MARKS READ platform-wide)
{"deviceId":"…","token":"…","op":"send","to":"…","body":"…"}  → sends as the owner, marked "via <device name>"
Before this route, every message endpoint was owner-Bearer and the glass could only be a face for the inbox (owner-side pusher). Now the device credential reaches the rail directly — worker-side the ops dispatch in-process to the existing DM handler classes, so send inherits every guardrail by construction (2000-char cap, 100/day, no self-DM, attachment allowlist). Probe receipts on the real token: bad token → 401 with no oracle, bad recipient → 404 through the full send chain, bad op / missing with → 400s. 10 s bound; a 503 is never masked as an empty inbox. The read side effect of thread is unchanged and sacred — fetch only on a real human open. The unread badge rides the heartbeat (opt-in wantUnread, above), and since 0.14.7 the firmware itself speaks this route: the on-device messages app fetches inbox and threads with the device token — it shipped as grammar v1 (an id namespace, not a new card type).

docs.title: Provisioning portal (device-side server, Nicla-compatible)
docs.text:
softAP  SSID tiny-XXXX (XXXX = FNV-1a over full MAC — Nicla lesson: suffix of serial collides)
        WPA2 key "tinysetup", 192.168.4.1
GET  /info  → {"kind":"reterminal-sticky","name":…,"mac":…,"version":…,"provisioned":bool}
POST /setup {device_id, token[, api, name], networks:[{ssid,key},…] | ssid,key}
        → save to NVS (merge semantics: upsert networks, scalars overwrite) → 200 → reboot
GET  /      → minimal HTML form (manual fallback)
The same portal has two entries (since 0.14.12): first boot (nothing in NVS, AP only) and rescue — after a 3-strike auth-halt the live STA widens to APSTA and raises the identical /setup → merge → reboot contract, so a re-issued token reaches a bricked-auth device with no serial cable and iOS onboarding code unchanged. STA stays associated in rescue, so a 401 that was a blip self-heals with the portal still up; the glass shows SSID + steps, a fallback card if APSTA itself fails (the panel is never silent), and re-entry is idempotent. One audited hole is on the fix queue: the rescue card's text sits at 468 bytes of a 512-byte buffer — close enough to blank the panel in exactly the path that exists because everything else failed; filed by the truncation sweep, honest here until fixed.

docs.title: Envelope command surface (what use_device reaches)
docs.text:
Envelopes are {type:'invoke', prompt}; prompt is parsed as <verb> [args], unknown text answers the help string (never silence). Replies ≤ 8000 B; images ride as hosted URLs. The per-verb reference with exact reply shapes lives in Commands (audited against the tree at 0.16.6-m14; the homepage pins the on-glass version):

verb does render_ui <card-json> render card → reply rendered card_id=<committed id> say <text> text card on the panel + ack chime, no network wait screenshot framebuffer → hosted PNG URL (render ground truth) page home\|status\|sensors\|settings\|wifi\|back\|next\|prev relay twin of stickyOS nav (parity rule) status machine-readable JSON + human summary field sensors [card] live I²C JSON; card also paints the sensors page miccheck [s] record → RMS/peak verdict live/SILENT (no upload) ask <text> owner-scoped agent turn via /api/devices/ask → card voice [s] PDM record → /api/media → ask with audioUrl (= AI button) sleep [s] reply → goodbye card → deep sleep (EXT1/timer wake) ota [channel] stage + sha-verify → reply → reboot into rollback-armed trial

Planned, not dispatched: image / stream (blit path exists in the renderer), wake (radio is off — button/timer only), reprovision (heartbeat-401 reopens the portal automatically).

docs.title: Card spec (render_ui) — as shipped
docs.text:
Types: text · list · kv · composite (≤4 parts) · qr (scannability-honest) · keyboard · menu · buttons (≤4, 56 px bottom bar) + title/footer/card_id on any card. Full spec with examples and the refresh policy: Cards.

Button tap → routed to the shell if the page owns it, else ui_tap device note → owner's activity feed → the agent answers with the next card. The screen is a conversation.

docs.title: Refresh policy
docs.text:
• buttons/text/list/kv → monochrome full (~600 ms class)
  • status-bar clock, stream frames → partial
  • photo/image cards with gray4:true → 4-level full (slowest, prettiest)
  • rate-limit: min 1.5 s between refreshes, coalesce bursts (queue, render last)

docs.title: Voice-ask pipeline
docs.text:
hold AI btn ≥1s → chime + "listening" partial-refresh glyph
→ PDM 16kHz/16-bit → PSRAM ring (cap 15s) → release → WAV
→ POST /api/media (device token) → audioUrl
→ POST /api/devices/ask {deviceId, token, audioUrl}     ← NEW backend route
→ backend: transcribe → owner-scoped agent turn → {text, card?}
→ card rendered; text also POSTed to /api/devices/transcript (durable)
Fallback until /ask ships: transcript + event, agent replies via relay envelope.

docs.title: Audio out — honesty section
docs.text: Hardware = magnetic buzzer on LEDC PWM. Tier 1 (ship): event chimes, melodies (RTTTL parser, ~1 KB). Tier 2 (experiment): 8-bit PCM via high-freq PWM duty modulation — known to produce barely intelligible speech on magnetic buzzers; we measure, we don't promise. Real TTS playback needs hardware we don't have; the honest framing is chimes + text-on-screen.

docs.title: Tasks / RTOS layout
docs.text:
task core prio job node 0 5 heartbeat/poll/dispatch (network-bound) render 1 6 canvas + refresh queue (SPI-bound, owns display) input 1 7 buttons ISR→queue, GT911 INT, touch regions audio 0 8 PDM capture bursts housekeeping 0 3 battery/RSSI sampling, status bar, sleep policy

Single event queue (AppEvent superset of demo's) so the demo's page framework keeps working underneath during bring-up.

docs.title: Provisioning UX
docs.text: First boot (or reprovision, or heartbeat-401): e-ink renders a setup card with QR (WIFI:S:tiny-XXXX;T:WPA;P:tinysetup;;) + SN + steps; softAP portal identical to Nicla's (/info advertises {kind:"reterminal-sticky", version, mac}). The tiny iOS app flow "add device → join AP → POST /setup {device_id, token, networks[]}" works with zero app changes — enrollment (POST /api/devices) already happens app-side.

docs.title: Security posture (inherited, non-negotiable)
docs.text:
• flash carries ONLY the device-scoped token (revocable; heartbeat-401 self-heals to portal)
  • OTA artifacts sha256-pinned, hosts pinned, staged to ota_1, trial-boot + self-test before commit; tiny_boot judges, tiny_ota only fetches
  • every socket has a timeout; no silent envelope execution (buzzer blip / LED)

docs.title: Build & release discipline (paid for on 2026-08-25, m12 night)
docs.text:
Three rules, each purchased with a real incident the same evening two agent lanes shared one checkout:

  1. Clean-worktree builds. An OTA image is only evidence if it reproduces from a committed sha: git worktree add /tmp/sticky-<label> <sha> and build there, never in the shared tree. Incident: an image built mid-edit shipped as 0.14.2-m12 — a label no commit carries — with page/tap answering but scroll unknown and a pre-M10 help string: three eras in one binary.
  2. Version labels are monotonic, even when the label was an accident. A published label is burned; the fix ships as a bump above it (0.14.3 above the phantom 0.14.2), never a re-use, so fw in a status reply names at most one image.
  3. Functional receipts over version fields. A deploy is verified by making the new surface answer (probe the verb, read the JSON, screenshot the glass), not by reading the version string — the version string is data inside the image and lies exactly when the build process does. Incident: deployed "0.14.2" failed its own superset claim (rotate yes, scroll no) under live probes. Structural fix (0.14.10): TINY_FW_COMMIT — a git sha injected at build time (not configure time; the stale-sha-on-incremental gap is the exact collision class being retired), with a --dirty suffix that is honest about uncommitted trees, surfaced as fw_commit in every status reply. Receipts still outrank strings — but the string can now prove ancestry instead of asserting it. (Fitting detail: version 0.14.10 itself exercises the numeric ver_cmp — lexicographic comparison would order 0.14.10 below 0.14.9.)

A fifth rule was purchased across three incidents in one night, all the same class — a shared worktree between agent lanes eats hunks between the editor and git add (00356b2's status hook, f6a46fb's torn tail committed with BUILD_EXIT=1, 32d0e14's clobbered feed that rollup constant-folded to null and dead-code-eliminated an entire feature out of a green bundle — the build was honest, the source was incomplete). The rule: claim a feature only after string-verifying it in the built artifact, never from the memory of writing it. Casualty #7 sharpened it: a unit test passed while the route it guarded was already gone, because the test exercised the function directly and never the route — test the surface a consumer touches, not the code you remember wiring to it — and verify at the right depth: a later crash-loop shipped through an ast.parse gate because the file was syntactically perfect and ordered wrong (a regex insert landed before the definitions it used); the gate now imports the module, because parse checks grammar while import runs the code, and only one of those is what production does. The same night added the edit-side twin: a version bump applied with sed silently did nothing (sed exits 0 whether or not it matched) and the lane read its pre-edit grep as if it were the result — two firmware versions rode out under one string until a self-caught collision commit (0.14.18) fixed it. Read back the state after the edit, never the intent before it — the same lane had written that hazard up twice for others before tripping it, which is the strongest argument that these are structural rules, not personal failings — and once, the race ran the other way: a sibling's live-wire field-name correction landed inside this documentation's own commit window, making the docs more correct than their author.

Rule six arrived the night fw_commit shipped, when the new field caught its first offender within hours: the glass was found running 9cdf43cf-dirty — the base commit a fine ancestor, but the -dirty delta is by definition unknown code, most plausibly a sibling lane's race hunk baked into the binary. The rule: never publish an image whose fw_commit is -dirty or unpushed — an artifact that cannot name its exact tree cannot be audited, rolled back to, or reproduced. A day later the field's one blind spot surfaced: the sha is read from git, but the source is read from the working tree — in a shared tree those are two different things. A "build green" receipt named a commit that cannot compile; it was green only because a sibling's repair sat uncommitted beside it. The fix is structural: publish builds happen in a clean detached worktree (git worktree add /tmp/wt <sha>), where describe --dirty must print a bare sha and no lane's half-finished hunks can ride along. And rule 6 gained its amendment: global --dirty trips on tracked logs and other lanes' docs edits that are not in the image — the precise gate is git status --porcelain -- firmware/ empty. Keep the rule, aim it at the right file set. 0.14.14 was the first publish built this way; 0.14.16 and 0.14.18 followed, each answering a bare clean fw_commit from the glass — a chain now, not a lucky first.

The same night also produced the advertise-only-what-dispatches invariant in its sharpest form: the heartbeat capability list and the dispatcher's branch table must be generated from the same truth, because they drifted twice — first in git (caught by review), then on glass (caught by probes).

And a fourth rule, from the night an OTA was deferred for a phantom finger: the glass is a shared, single-user surface — probe etiquette applies. An agent lane announces on-glass probe sequences before running them, restores the previous page after, and stands down entirely when the events feed shows a human actively using the device. With one correction paid for the same night: a tap in the feed is not proof of a finger. The relay tap verb produces events indistinguishable from touch — the builder once stood down for hours deferring to a "human" that was another lane's probe. Attribute activity before deferring to it. Read-only verbs (status, sensors, bare scroll) stay fair game — they answer without repainting anything.

The fifth rule was minted by a near-miss, not an incident: an OTA must prove ancestry before it publishes. A version number ordering is not enough — a build named 0.14.5 was minutes from publishing after 0.14.6 was already on glass (the builder's tree predated the hotfix), which would have silently rolled back the label-sniff security fix while looking like a routine update. The check is mechanical: the commit currently deployed must be an ancestor of the tree being flashed (git merge-base --is-ancestor <on-glass> <build>), and "what is on glass" comes from a live status probe, never from memory. The supervisor's block landed with the build already staged. The audit that followed located the root cause in code: the device's own trigger is direction-blind (strcmp difference, not comparison), so the firmware would install a stale pointer as faithfully as a fresh one — integrity checked, direction unchecked. The fix shipped as 0.14.9: numeric ver_cmp (unparseable = incomparable = refuse, fail closed) with a loud force:"1" override — and the publisher-side ancestry check stays in force. Two guards, one on each side of the wire.

docs.title: RECOVERY — how to get back to stock, always
docs.text: Rule zero: the ESP32-S3 cannot be bricked by an app flash. The ROM serial bootloader lives in mask ROM. If the firmware is broken, hold the reset-hole strapping combo (or just let a bad app crash-loop — esptool can still sync during resets) and talk to /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881.

docs.title: Path 1 — our byte-exact dump (preferred: restores THIS unit, NVS/SN/calibration included)
docs.text:
Created on arrival day from the as-shipped device:

# dump (how recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin was made) — ~45 min at default baud
# NOTE: 921600 fails through the USB hub chain ("serial noise"); default 115200 is reliable
~/.tiny/pypi/bin/esptool --port /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881 read-flash 0 0x2000000 stock-firmware-32MB.bin

# restore
~/.tiny/pypi/bin/esptool --port /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881 --baud 460800 write-flash 0 stock-firmware-32MB.bin

sha256 of the dump is recorded in recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin.sha256 (bin itself is gitignored, 32MB — lives on cagatay-mac and should be copied to the Mac mini as a second host).

docs.title: Path 2 — official factory image (browser, zero tooling)
docs.text:
Seeed ships stock as a playground-registry integration: sticky-factory v1.1.0, one full 32MB image at offset 0, sha256 8b149c809b7c07c680a59ab5621d7bd29ca85a8c1c9e9060b0040b387b4517e4 (recovery/factory-manifest.json).

docs.title: RESEARCH — everything we verified before writing a line of firmware
docs.text: 2026-08-25, tiny. Sources: live device on this desk, official docs (seeedstudio.com/sticky/docs), Seeed demo sources (vendor/), the playground registry, ~/strands-nicla firmware, ~/tinyai-id backend source.

docs.title: 1. The device on the desk
docs.text:
Verified with esptool against the real unit (arrived 2026-08-25, a day early):

  • ESP32-S3 QFN56 rev v0.2, dual core 240MHz + LP core, WiFi + BT5 LE
  • 8MB embedded PSRAM (AP_3v3), 32MB quad flash (Winbond, ef/4019)
  • MAC b8:1f:3f:d7:23:60, crystal 40MHz
  • USB bridge: WCH CH343 → /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881
  • 921600 read-flash failed twice through the hub chain ("serial noise or corruption"); 115200 is reliable. Expect ~45 min for a full 32MB dump; use 460800 for app-size writes and fall back on error.
  • Stock firmware serial console at 115200 printed garbage — stock log baud unknown, irrelevant once we own the firmware.

docs.title: 2. Official pin map (hardware-overview, cross-checked w/ community + demo pin_config.h)
docs.text: Subsystem Pins Notes e-paper SPI2 SCK13 MOSI/SDI14 CS15 DC16 RST17 BUSY18 EN47 SSD1677-class, 800×480, 1-bit + 4-gray modes microSD shares SPI2, CS8 never drive concurrently with display transfer Touch GT911 I²C0: SCL2 SDA3 INT21 RST41 EN42 y-axis mirrored in community firmware (800-y) — verify on ours Sensor bus I²C1: SCL0 SDA1 SHT40 + LSM6DS3TR-C (INT=GPIO7, now official) + PCF8563 + BQ27220@0x55 PDM mic CLK19 DATA20 ⚠ deep-sleep wake pin-mux bug, §6 Mic power GPIO38 (TPS22916 load switch) community-sourced; demo's sticky_microphone is ground truth Buttons AI/PWR=4 (EXT1 wake), UP=5, DOWN=6 Buzzer PWM GPIO48 official USB serial TX43 RX44 Power latch HOLD=45 (keep HIGH), LOCK=46 community source only — official page omits it; demo's sticky_power.cpp is ground truth. Get this wrong → device powers off at boot.

docs.title: 3. Seeed's ESP-IDF demos are a complete HAL (vendor/)
docs.text:
Sticky_dashboard_demo (ESP-IDF v5.4) contains everything hardware-touching we would otherwise write blind:

  • components/: seeed_epaper (the display driver!), gt911, bq27220, button (espressif iot_button), debug_logging
  • main/devices/: sticky_display|touch|microphone|buzzer|power|imu|sht40|rtc|sdcard|battery|charger|buttons — clean C++ modules over the components
  • main/board/: board_init() = power latch + shared I²C1 bus + SD defaults; modules reuse board_sensor_i2c_bus()
  • main/app|pages|ui/: AppState/AppEvent page framework + Canvas
  • Display API — three refresh modes, exactly the primitives render_ui needs:
  • sticky_display_refresh() — 4-gray full (~slowest, prettiest)
  • sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() — 1-bit full
  • sticky_display_refresh_partial() — 1-bit partial (status-bar clock pattern)
  • the driver applies a 180° rotation on refresh — framebuffer orientation matters for the screenshot tool
  • Integration patterns (esp-pages doc): read-on-page-entry (SHT40/battery), background monitor (IMU), capture-on-request (mic), input events (button/touch → AppEvent)
  • Deep sleep: AI button long-press → render sleep page → monochrome refresh → deep sleep; EXT1 wake on GPIO4

Decision: we do NOT rewrite the HAL. firmware/ reuses vendor/Sticky_dashboard_demo/components via EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS and adapts the main/devices layer; our work is the tiny/* layer above it.

docs.title: 4. tiny.technology device contract (read from ~/tinyai-id source — exact, not guessed)
docs.text:
Ported 1:1 from the Nicla (~/strands-nicla/firmware/tiny_node.py mirrors tiny-tech/src/mesh/relay-poller.ts):

Verb Route Auth Shape enroll POST /api/devices session (app/CLI does it) {name, platform?, kind?, capabilities?} → {device_id, device_token} token returned once adopt POST /api/devices/adopt session {deviceId} → rotated token (old token dies instantly) heartbeat POST /api/devices/heartbeat device token in body {deviceId, token, capabilities} every 30 s; 401 = revoked → reopen provisioning portal poll PUT /api/devices/relay device token in body {deviceId, token, max:5} every 5 s → {messages:[{id, payload}]}, envelopes {type:'invoke', prompt} reply PATCH /api/devices/relay device token in body {deviceId, token, inReplyTo, payload} — payload = serialized JSON string {result[, images:[{url,format}]]} ≤ 8000 bytes media POST /api/media device token in body {deviceId, token, data:<b64>, contentType} → hosted URL. Nicla streams this raw-socket to avoid buffering; on ESP32-S3 with 8MB PSRAM we can buffer + esp_http_client transcript POST /api/devices/transcript device token in body {deviceId, token, text, label?, audioUrl?, durationS?} — outlives the 1 h relay sweep OTA pointer PUT /api/firmware/manifest device token in body {deviceId, token, channel} → {bundle:{url, sha256}} — pollable channel → manifest → artifacts

Principles inherited from the Nicla (they're in the source comments for good reasons): - the device token is the only credential in flash — scoped, revocable; never the account bearer - every HTTP call gets a hard timeout (Nicla went silent 4.5 min on one hung socket) - no agent runs on-board — a command table maps envelope prompts to hardware actions; flash an LED/buzzer blip per executed envelope (nothing runs silently) - OTA: manifest pinned by sha256, artifact hosts pinned, downloader may never approve its own download (boot/trial/commit logic stays out of the OTA path)

docs.title: 5. The one backend gap: "ask tiny" for a phoneless device
docs.text:
Nicla voice flow leans on the paired iPhone to record + transcribe on-device, then POST /transcript. The Sticky has no phone. Needed in ~/tinyai-id (we own it):

POST /api/devices/ask {deviceId, token, audioUrl | text} → worker: transcribe (audio case) → run owner-scoped agent turn → reply {text, card?} (card = render_ui spec). Falls out of existing pieces: media upload already device-authed, transcript route shows the auth pattern, agent turns exist for every other surface. Until it lands, the fallback is: device uploads WAV + posts transcript-request event; a scheduled agent answers via relay envelope (slower, works today).

docs.title: 6. Known hardware traps (from community voice-companion firmware — same physical device)
docs.text:
1. Deep-sleep wake kills the PDM mic: ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for USB-Serial-JTAG on wake. Fix at boot, before I²S init: USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable=0; gpio_reset_pin(19/20); cycle mic rail (GPIO38 LOW 150 ms).
  2. Power latch: GPIO45 must go HIGH early in boot or the device just turns off.
  3. GT911 y-mirror: touch y arrives flipped (800 - y) in the community build — calibrate against our own driver during M2.
  4. Shared SPI2: SD and e-paper transfers must be serialized.

docs.title: 7. Recovery research (the "how do we un-brick" answer)
docs.text:
• ROM download mode is unkillable: hold BOOT-equivalent (the reset hole / strapping pin) → USB bootloader, esptool always works. A bad app cannot brick the S3.
  • Official factory image: playground registry sticky-factory, mode flash, v1.1.0 = one 33,292,288-byte image at offset 0 (sha256 8b149c…17e4), browser-flashable (Chrome/Edge WebSerial) with an erase option, or by hand with esptool. Older versions 0.2.1–1.0.1 as GitHub releases with per-manifest sha256.
  • Our dump: full 32MB read-flash of the exact as-shipped unit (includes its NVS: factory calibration, SN, any per-device binding) — recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin. The official image restores firmware; our dump restores this unit byte-for-byte.
  • Re-pairing after restore: stock firmware re-enters Seeedash pairing; the SN survives in its own partition (part of why we dump all 32MB, not just the app).

docs.title: 8. Stock firmware UX (what we replace, and the bar to clear)
docs.text:
Seeedash app: BLE pairing (SN shown on screen) → 2.4GHz Wi-Fi → device runs phone-free; OTA via app. Buttons: AI 3 s = on, both page 1 s = off, AI 1 s = voice note, any = wake; 2 min idle → sleep. Apps: Notes/Weather/Clock/Photos/Designs/AI-usage. Fonts via microSD fonts/*.fpack.

Our provisioning replaces BLE-pairing with the Nicla AP portal (tiny-XXXX / tinysetup / 192.168.4.1, GET /info, POST /setup) so the existing tiny iOS onboarding works unchanged. BLE provisioning can come later as a nicety (NimBLE NUS), not a dependency.

docs.title: 9. Sizing sanity
docs.text:
• Framebuffer 800×480: 1-bit = 48 KB, 2-bit (4-gray) = 96 KB — trivial in 8MB PSRAM; keep both a work canvas and a shadow copy for partial-refresh diffs and screenshots.
  • Screenshot as 8-bit grayscale BMP = 384 KB → b64 ≈ 512 KB upload, fine over Wi-Fi; 1-bit BMP = 48 KB. Start with 8-bit BMP (zero-dependency encoder), consider PNG (miniz) later.
  • Mic: 16 kHz/16-bit mono WAV, 10 s = 320 KB — buffers in PSRAM, uploads in seconds.
  • Partition plan for 32MB: nvs(24K) otadata(8K) phy(4K) factory(4M) ota_0(4M) ota_1(4M) assets-spiffs(rest ~19M) — factory slot holds our recovery-capable base build; OTA A/B for tiny_ota.

docs.title: 10. Open questions for bring-up (M0/M1 will answer)
docs.text:
1. Does the demo build unmodified on IDF v5.4 + our unit? (M0 gate)
  2. Real partial-refresh latency + ghosting budget → render_ui refresh policy
  3. GT911 orientation on our unit
  4. Buzzer PCM experiment: LEDC @ ~40 kHz carrier, 8-bit duty modulation — audible speech or noise? (fun, non-blocking)
  5. Wi-Fi power draw vs 750 mAh: relay poll every 5 s will not survive days on battery → light-sleep between polls, or lengthen poll interval when on battery (heartbeat carries battery %, backend can adapt)

docs.title: ROADMAP — loop-driven delivery plan
docs.text: Executed by tiny as a worker loop + supervisor loop (two slots). Each milestone has a hard gate — the loop may not advance past a gate without the evidence named there. Flash/monitor happen on cagatay-mac (/dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881); the loop runs on this machine and has the port.

docs.title: Ground rules for the loops
docs.text:
• Never flash before recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin + .sha256 exist and match (M0 includes verifying the dump that is currently being read).
  • Prefer 460800 baud for writes; on "serial noise/corruption" drop to 115200. Never two esptool/monitor processes on the port at once.
  • Commit per green step; push per milestone; journal decisions in docs/JOURNAL.md.
  • Vendor sources are read-only reference — adaptations are COPIES into firmware/.
  • Anything touching ~/tinyai-id (the /api/devices/ask route) gets its own branch + cagatay review before deploy; the firmware must keep its fallback path.

docs.text:

  • verify commits are pushed; escalate to cagatay (use_notify) on: gate failure ×2, any flash-erase beyond app partitions, anything touching tinyai-id deploy
  • keep docs/JOURNAL.md honest — every gate needs evidence (measurement, photo, or transcript), not assertion

docs.title: THINKING.md — a deep-dive session on what stickyOS actually is
docs.text: 2026-08-25, late evening. Written by the main-session tiny after one bring-up day: 12 OTAs, a keyboard on glass, an iOS remote in cagatay's pocket, two loops still running. This is the thinking the commit log doesn't hold — read it before making the next big call.

docs.title: 1. What we actually built today (get the category right)
docs.text:
The Sticky is not a display peripheral and not an IoT gadget. It's the fifth embodiment of one agent identity (phone, web, camera-necklace, voice-necklace, and now a wall). The category test from the MHS essay applies verbatim: a robot is anything that can introduce itself — readable state, changeable state with declared limits, callable procedures, announcements. The Sticky passed that test by ~18:00 today: status (readable), page/render_ui (changeable, bounded), verbs advertised in a capability list (declared), device_note events (announcements).

What makes it different from its four siblings: it's the first embodiment that is a PLACE, not a companion. The phone travels, the necklace is worn, the web follows the login. The Sticky is bolted to a wall in one room of one home. Every design decision downstream should flow from that: it serves whoever stands in front of it, its content should assume the household, and its latency contract is glanceable, not interactive-first.

docs.title: 2. The physics is the design language (stop fighting the panel)
docs.text:
Every failed UI idea today failed the same way: pretending the panel is an LCD. The working ideas all scheduled around the panel. Write the latency budget on the wall:

Event Budget Mechanism Tap acknowledged < 50ms buzzer (audio is the fast lane) Tap visually confirmed 300–500ms partial refresh, region-sized Page change 1–2s full refresh (the metronome) Relay verb round-trip 5–15s poll cadence + agent turn Ask with tools 10–60s backend agent loop

The deep principle: on e-ink, UI is a series of commitments, not a stream of frames. A phone UI animates toward a state; the Sticky declares states. That's why the notification model matters so much (§4): interruptions are expensive when every repaint costs 1–2s of visible flicker, so the OS must own when the glass changes, and everything else queues. Same reason double-tap and drag were rejected in the touch audit — they're promises the panel can't keep. Design verbs the panel CAN keep: tap, swipe-as-command (not swipe-as-scroll-physics), long-press, and time (cards that age gracefully).

Corollary nobody should forget: audio is the low-latency channel. The buzzer is the only sub-100ms output this device has. Chimes, clicks, and error tones aren't polish — they're the half of the interaction loop the panel physically cannot provide.

docs.title: 3. "Phone replacement" — deconstructed honestly
docs.text:
Cagatay's framing ("mobile phone replacement", "stickyOS to go") is directionally right and literally wrong, and the difference is the product:

A phone is four things: always-with-you, an input surface, a notification funnel, and an identity token. The Sticky can be three of them at home — it will never be always-with-you (that's the necklace's job). So the honest thesis:

The Sticky replaces the phone in the room it lives in. Reaching for your phone to ask a question, check a status, send a message while standing in your kitchen — that's the behavior it deletes. The phone becomes the mobile terminal; the Sticky is the domestic one.

This resolves the tension in the directives: iOS design parity (§6 of phase 3) isn't about making the Sticky be an iPhone — it's about making it recognizably the same tiny so switching rooms doesn't mean switching mental models. Same pages, same names, same hierarchy; different physics.

It also predicts the endgame (§7): one Sticky is a domestic terminal; N stickies are a house-scale UI. Kitchen shows the morning brief, door shows weather + calendar on the way out, desk shows the build status. The fleet already has the primitives (per-device relay, cards, presence). "stickyOS to go" ends with the home being the device.

docs.title: 4. Architecture tensions that will bite (ranked, with positions taken)
docs.text:
T1 — Poll vs push. The 5s relay poll is both the latency floor (§2 table) and the battery ceiling. 750mAh with always-on Wi-Fi + 5s HTTPS polls is a days-not-weeks device; the audit's adaptive-poll directive helps but doesn't change the shape. Position: keep polling for v1 (it's simple, NAT-proof, and proven today), but the M-next experiment is long-poll: hold the GET open 30–60s server-side, reply on envelope arrival. Same firmware surface (esp_http_client), near-instant push, and fewer TLS handshakes than 5s polling. Wake-on-lift (IMU) then gates the whole radio: asleep = 60s cadence, lifted/touched = long-poll. That combination is the difference between "charge it weekly" and "why is it dead again".

T2 — Who owns the glass. Today a remote render_ui stomps whatever page the user is on — already directed to fix via the notification model, but state the deeper rule: stickyOS needs a focus concept. The local shell is the compositor; remote content is a request for focus, not a seizure of it. Home screen = remote cards land immediately (it's ambient). Any other page = dot + notifications queue. The one exception: safety/alarm class cards (a priority field the card spec doesn't have yet — add it before someone builds an alert feature on a queue that can silently defer it).

T3 — The verb grammar is now a 3-consumer contract (dashboard, iOS panel, relay/agent). It's held together by string prefixes and shared discipline. Before phase 3 widens it (messages, images, scroll state), pin it: a grammar_version in the status reply + the capability list already advertised. The iOS panel and dashboard check it and degrade politely. Cheap now, impossible to retrofit after a fleet of stickies exists.

T4 — Keystroke privacy set a precedent — name it. The keyboard's k: taps never leave the device. Generalize: local-only zones — input surfaces whose events are consumed by the shell and never posted upstream. The Wi-Fi password keyboard is one; a future PIN pad, a "private note" composer. Make it a card attribute ("local": true), not a keyboard special case. This is the kind of promise that, kept structurally, becomes a reason to trust the whole fleet.

T5 — The agent is the OS vendor, and it ships 12 times a day. Today's cadence (build → OTA → verify-on-glass → journal) worked because the rollback judge (first heartbeat 200 marks valid) and sha pinning were built in M6, before velocity. What's missing at this speed: a canary ritual for the day there are two stickies (update one, watch a full heartbeat+verb cycle, then the rest) and a factory-image discipline (one known-good build burned to the recovery partition quarterly). Velocity is only a virtue while the device can always crawl home. Related honesty: today's "version-string lie" (0.7.0 reporting before m7a code shipped) is the failure mode of agent-speed shipping — the fix (behavior probes over version fields) belongs in the supervisor's permanent checklist, not just today's memory.

T6 — The provisioning gap is the shippability gap. Everything else on the roadmap is polish; softAP provisioning is the difference between "cagatay's device" and "a device". It's correctly next in the builder queue. Hold the line: no new feature work should jump it (keyboard already exists — the portal can reuse it, which is the elegant closure: the first thing the on-glass keyboard provisions is the device itself).

docs.title: 5. The most interesting thing here (the part worth a blog post)
docs.text:
stickyOS is being developed almost entirely by agent loops — builder writes firmware, supervisor verifies on glass, main session translates human intent into directives, and the product itself is a surface for the same agent. The loop closes fully when the Sticky's own ask verb reaches the full toolset (phase-3 #1): at that point the device can be asked to describe, diagnose, and file issues against its own firmware — the machine introduces itself not just to the network but to its own development process.

That's the same recursion as the necklace essay (an agent designs a body, a printer makes it, the object is where the next agent lives) — but sharper: the Sticky is the first tiny embodiment whose operating system is a nightly artifact of the agent that inhabits it. Bench discipline is what keeps that from being scary instead of delightful: every claim journaled with evidence, every OTA reversible, every "it works" backed by a screenshot of the glass or a human finger. Today produced multiple instances of the pattern "the machine said done; the glass disagreed; the glass won." Keep the glass winning.

docs.title: 6. Ranked risks (what actually threatens the mission)
docs.text:
1. Orientation surgery (M10.O) — touches the renderer's deepest invariant (canvas/touch/screenshot agreement, verified in audit). Sequenced correctly (after Wi-Fi keyboard). Demand the arrow-up test card in all 4 orientations × touch hit-test before it merges.
  2. Battery honesty — no measurement exists yet of real draw. Before adaptive polling is designed, spend one loop iteration measuring: current at 5s poll idle, at long-poll idle, asleep. Design against numbers, not vibes (the bench rule: an artifact declares what it IS).
  3. Font/UTF-8 debt — every text surface built before the real font lands inherits ASCII-fold shame ("Cagatay" on the glass of a Turkish speaker's kitchen). It's scheduled; don't let it slip behind feature work again.
  4. Single-unit fleet — every OTA bets the only device. Mitigated by rollback + recovery doc; properly fixed by the second unit (canary, §T5).
  5. Context debt in the loops — builder loop v1 died of a 15-min inline wait; v2 learned reply-then-act. The lesson generalizes: the loops' own working discipline is part of the architecture now and belongs in LOOP_BRIEF.md, not tribal memory.

docs.title: 7. Where this goes (12-month shape, so near-term calls aim somewhere)
docs.text:
• 1 Sticky (now): domestic terminal, stickyOS phases 2–3, battery truth.
  • 2–3 Stickies: canary OTA ritual; rooms get roles; presence-aware cards (the kitchen one knows it's morning); the notification model becomes a house-wide router ("show this where someone is standing").
  • Sticky as product: softAP portal + factory image + the enrollment story make it giftable. The e-ink tile becomes the calm face of tiny — the anti-doomscroll surface: no feed, no infinite anything, cards that age.
  • The MHS rhyme: a Sticky declares bounds (refresh budget, local-only zones, battery gates) in its capability surface. It's the same thesis at domestic scale: safety and honesty as properties of the device, not paragraphs in a prompt. When the embargo lifts and the essay ships, the Sticky is quietly its best demo: any machine can introduce itself — even a fridge magnet.

Filed by the main session. Supervisor v2: hold T2 (focus/priority field), T3 (grammar_version) and risk #2 (battery measurement) against the phase-3 queue — they're cheap now and expensive later. Everything else is direction, not work items.

docs.title: UX Spec — the stickyOS interaction contract
docs.text:
Owner: the product-designer loop. Version 1.6 (2026-08-26) — §15 chat conversation surface (ask lifecycle, follow-up context, DM consent gate); v1.5 added §13 sound rules, §14 anim law, §7 settings IA v2. This file is the single source of truth for how the Sticky feels. The builder implements it; verdicts against it land in ANSWERS.md. Every rule carries a WHY, and every rule carries a status: SPECIFIED → BUILT → VERIFIED-ON-GLASS (only an owner-loop screenshot or probe receipt flips the last one).

Seed law from cagatay (2026-08-26, verbatim intent — everything else expands it):

  1. Swipe bottom → up = HOME, from anywhere.
  2. Swipe left → right = previous / back.
  3. Gestures are context-dependent — in the gallery, horizontal swipes mean previous/next image, not page nav.
  4. Settings must be truly editable on-device.

docs.title: 0. Physics and vocabulary the spec obeys
docs.text:
• Full refresh ~1–2 s; partial ~300–500 ms; ghosting after ~20 partials; ~2 Hz animation ceiling. A gesture may therefore trigger at most one panel-visible response, and the ack must be felt before it is seen (buzzer <60 ms, visual <500 ms) — the "touch feels dead" incident (TOUCH_AUDIT) is the founding lesson.
  • Coordinate spaces: touch and screenshot live in panel space (800×480 landscape, invariant under rotation). Gestures are interpreted in layout space — "up" means visually up in the current rotation, exactly as the M12 scroll gesture already does (tiny_display_scroll_gesture maps the vector). WHY: a human swipes relative to what they see, not to the panel's wiring.
  • Feedback vocabulary (three words, never more):
  • single blip + visual ack = accepted, something happened;
  • double short blip = recognized but refused — a dead end, and the double blip IS the explanation a 2 Hz panel can afford;
  • silence = below thresholds, not a gesture. Nothing else is silent. WHY: on e-ink the sound arrives 10× sooner than any pixel can.

docs.title: 1. Zones and thresholds (layout space)
docs.text:
name definition why tap slop movement < 24 px (shipped) finger roll ≠ swipe swipe travel ≥ 120 px dominant axis scroll steps and slips stay distinct axis dominance dominant ≥ 2× the other axis diagonal = ambiguous = silence bottom band start-y in the last 56 px of layout height (= the touch-bar strip) edge-origin marks NAV intent; a button tap moves <24 px so the two can never collide left band start-x in the first 48 px of layout width iOS back-swipe muscle memory long-press ≥ 750 ms, < slop movement, fire AT threshold with blip reserved (context menu, phase 2)

The conflict rule, decided: edge-originated swipes are NAV; mid-content swipes are CONTENT. Bottom-band-up = home even on a scrollable card — a scroll swipe naturally starts mid-body, and content under the touch bar is reachable by scrolling down from above. WHY: one spatial rule resolves every home-vs-scroll ambiguity without modes, and it is defensible in one sentence.

docs.title: 2. The gesture grammar (gesture × context → action)
docs.text:
Contexts: ring page (home/status/sensors/settings root), pushed card (wifi list, message thread, ble, any relay-rendered card), gallery, keyboard, streaming answer, locked (pocket, P-1).

gesture ring page pushed card gallery keyboard streaming locked bottom-band swipe ↑ HOME (law #1) HOME HOME HOME (= cancel, don't save) blip-defer¹ ignored² left-band swipe → back = ring prev BACK (pop) (law #2) BACK (exit gallery) dead-end ‼ (keys own the glass) blip-defer¹ ignored² mid-content swipe ← / → ring next / prev → = back, ← = dead-end ‼ next / prev IMAGE (law #3) silence³ blip-defer¹ ignored² mid-content swipe ↑ / ↓ scroll if overflowing (M12, shipped — do not break), else dead-end ‼ same caption show/hide reserved; v1 dead-end ‼ silence³ auto-scroll owns the tail¹ ignored² tap on button/row/key activate (shipped) activate button parity (Prev/Next/Back) type (ack = value line) blip-defer¹ ignored² tap on empty canvas silence (logged) silence toggle caption silence blip-defer¹ ignored² long-press (touch) reserved, phase 2 — silence until then ← ← ← ← ignored²

‼ dead-end = double blip, nothing moves. WHY: a recognized gesture that does nothing must say it was heard, or the panel reads as broken.

¹ Streaming answer: the stream owns the display (STREAMING_UI rule 7); no tap regions exist mid-stream by design. Every touch gets a single blip and is discarded — acknowledged, not obeyed. The ONE exit is physical: long-press AI (2 s) aborts the stream (stream_end, append "[interrupted]") and goes home. WHY: a stream is bounded (≤30 s + stall watchdog), so deferring touch is predictable; but no state may ever hold the device with zero exits, and the exit must work through fabric and gloves — hence a button, not a gesture.

² Locked (pocket, P-1): touch fully ignored, no blips (a buzzing pocket is noise, and buzzer-on-every-fabric-brush drains the 750 mAh pack). No voice capture starts while locked. Unlock = hold UP + DOWN together 1 s → single blip + wake card. WHY: a chord is the one input fabric cannot forge.

³ Keyboard silence exception: horizontal/vertical swipes over the key area are silence, not dead-end — typing drift would otherwise double-blip constantly. The keyboard's own cancel/ok keys and the bottom-band home swipe are its exits.

Rotation invariant: the table above is layout-space; the router maps through the current rotation before classifying (the scroll gesture already does; NAV must ride the same transform). A gesture mid-rotation-commit is dropped like a tap on a changed card-gen.

docs.title: 3. Physical button parity (accessibility + gloves + pocket)
docs.text:
Every gesture verb has a button path — gestures are an optimization, never the only door:

intent gesture button path home bottom-band ↑ long-press AI (shipped) back / prev left-band → UP click on pushed card = back; on ring = prev page (shipped ring) next mid ← DOWN click (shipped ring; = next image in gallery) scroll mid ↑/↓ UP/DOWN on overflowing card (shipped) ask tap Speak / hold AI hold AI (shipped) abort stream — (deliberately none) long-press AI 2 s unlock — (deliberately none) UP+DOWN chord 1 s

WHY: the audit's P-1 pocket case and glove/winter use both reduce to "the three keys must be able to do everything destructive or rescuing."

docs.title: 4. Navigation model — ring and stack, reconciled
docs.text:
• The ring is the set of top-level pages: home ▸ status ▸ sensors ▸ settings (+ gallery when it lands). Ring moves (UP/DOWN, horizontal swipes on a ring page) replace the stack top — depth stays 1. WHY: cycling must never build a 47-deep history of status pages.
  • Opens push: settings→wifi, chats→thread, any keyboard, any relay card the shell didn't originate. Back pops. Home clears to [home].
  • A relay render_ui card arrives as a pushed card — back from it returns to what the human was doing. WHY: a remote agent may interject but never steal the human's place.
  • Stack depth 8 (shipped) is ample; overflow drops the oldest non-home entry.

docs.title: 5. Feedback rules (the 500 ms contract)
docs.text:
1. Buzz before anything that can block; visual ack within 500 ms via region partial (shipped invert-ack) — except keyboard keys, where the value line IS the ack (shipped).
  2. Dead ends double-blip (new). Locked state never blips (new).
  3. An action that will take >2 s (ask, wifi join, image fetch) must leave a pending mark on the glass within 500 ms (streaming chrome, "joining…" row, caption "fetching…"). WHY: e-ink cannot spin a spinner; a written word is our progress indicator.
  4. Every refusal names its reason on the glass (house honesty rule).

docs.title: 6. Cards — typography & hierarchy rules
docs.text:
• One idea per card; title ≤ ~28 chars before fold; body is the only scrollable region; footer is metadata, never content; ≤4 buttons.
  • Contrast ladder: Black on White for content, DarkGray for chrome/hairlines, LightGray fills only for "user bubble" / selection. WHY: 4-gray is a hierarchy budget, not a palette.
  • Streaming chat chrome per STREAMING_UI layer 4 (user bubble right/LightGray, assistant left/outlined; caret only while bytes may arrive). Bubble max-width = 70% of body width (v1.2, R-3; VERIFIED-ON-GLASS 0.16.8 batch #8: 508/752=67.6% wrapped, short bubbles shrink-to-fit): shrink-to-fit when short, wrap at 70% when long — a 28-char column on an 800 px panel reads as a receipt, not a conversation.
  • Emoji/glyphs with no 4-gray rendering are stripped in chat bubbles, never folded to "?" (v1.3, R-4; VERIFIED-ON-GLASS 0.16.8 batch #8 by 16px differential — 👋 gone, 東京 keeps ??): "Hey! ?" is a different sentence than "Hey! 👋" — absence is honest, substitution changes tone. Content characters keep the fold-table "?".

docs.title: 7. Settings — information architecture (law #4: truly editable)
docs.text:
Settings root becomes a menu (rows, not a kv dump; current kv view moves to About):

Settings
├─ 🔕 Snooze     → FIRST ROW, one tap cycles: Off → 1h → until-wake → forever.
│                 Row note shows the countdown/state. Mutes all LOCAL sounds
│                 (§13 tier L); never mutes owner-hand `play`. WHY first: the
│                 owner's own words — "cut the voice of the beeps when i click
│                 somewhere" — and the acceptance is ≤2 taps from anywhere
│                 (home → Settings → Snooze).
├─ Sounds       → volume tier (duty): Soft / Normal · per-event toggles:
│                 tap / ack / error / dm / boot jingle
├─ Display      → rotation: Auto / 0 / 90 / 180 / 270 (lock = manual mode,
│                 same semantics as `rotate` verb) · theme: Light / Dark (invert)
│                 · glance-on-wake: On / Off
├─ Wi-Fi        → networks list: join (keyboard), forget, move-up priority;
│                 stored nets in NVS; passwords render as dots, always
├─ Agent        → thinkers list (M-A7: prompt · every X · last-run · on/off,
│                 [New thinker] → keyboard → interval menu) · ask history On/Off
├─ Power        → sleep timeout: 2 / 5 / 15 min / Never · eco threshold display
├─ Lock         → pocket lockout: Auto (IMU) / Off · shows unlock chord hint
└─ About        → fw, commit, channel, device id, mac, ssid/rssi, battery health

Every editable row states its current value in the row note (menu note field, shipped) so the glass never hides state behind a tap. Toggles commit on tap with single blip + row re-render (partial) + an NVS scalar + a set <key> <val> relay twin, so every on-glass edit is also scriptable. WHY: a settings page that requires a phone is an admission the device isn't sovereign — and a setting without a relay twin is untestable by the verdict rail.

docs.title: 8. Gallery — interaction model (with builder M-A4)
docs.text:
• v1 is a single-image pager, newest first: open → latest image full-bleed (1-bit, server-dithered), caption + glance bar toggled by empty-canvas tap.
  • Horizontal swipes / UP/DOWN = prev/next (law #3). Bottom-band ↑ = home. Left-band → = back. On-glass Prev/Next/Back buttons for parity.
  • Every image lands with a full refresh (an image IS a new page; partial ghosting over a photo is unacceptable).
  • Ends of the roll are dead ends (double blip), never wraparound. WHY: a loop of N images with 1–2 s page turns makes "am I at the start?" unanswerable.
  • Offline (P-2): cached rasters stay browsable; glance bar shows w-; an uncached image says "not cached — offline", never a blank frame.

docs.title: 9. Error & offline states (what the device SAYS)
docs.text: state the glass says why wifi down glance w-; current card persists (e-ink superpower) ambient truth, no modal panic ask fails / 422 "didn't catch that" card (shipped) / error card naming the HTTP reason a refusal names its reason ask never left the device (transport, st ≤ 0) "couldn't reach tiny — your question was NOT sent; try again" + free-heap in footer. The word "Backend" is forbidden here an error message must name the true culprit; "Backend said -1" attributes to the backend words it never said (owner-hit P1, 2026-08-26 02:5xZ) stream stalls "[stream stalled]" appended, caret removed (shipped) a cut answer must say it is cut relay silent nothing changes on glass device-initiated surfaces only; silence upstream isn't the human's problem image fetch fails "couldn't fetch image ()" honest-void never a half-blitted frame auth-halt rescue portal card + QR (shipped) recovery without a cable

docs.title: 11. Pocket lockout — the state machine (P-1, safety-critical)
docs.text:
Pocket-carry's one unforgivable failure: fabric holds the AI button, 15 s of audio records and uploads. Lockout is therefore a SAFETY feature, not a convenience.

States: UNLOCKED ⇄ LOCKED (no third state; "locking…" does not exist on e-ink).

Entry to LOCKED (any one): - IMU: face-down ≥ 3 s, OR sustained walking-motion signature ≥ 5 s while no touch for 30 s (thresholds are firmware constants, tuned on-device, named in code) - Manual: Settings ▸ Lock, or a future button chord

While LOCKED: - Touch controller: PHYSICAL (GT911) events discarded at the router (not deshielded per-page). Relay-synthetic tap/swipe still route — owner's authenticated remote reach, same class as say/render_ui; fabric cannot forge them (batch-#9 ruling). - AI button: hold does NOT start voice capture — the one rule that is the point. Short-press wakes the glass to the glance card (§12) with a lock glyph. - UP/DOWN: page nothing; they are the unlock chord only - Buzzer: chirps still allowed (notification while pocketed = the product working) - Relay verbs: STILL ANSWER (status/screenshot/say/render_ui) — lockout guards the device's own inputs, not the owner's remote reach. EVERY mic path refuses while locked with an honest sentence — voice AND miccheck (D-UX5: the rule is "no capture while locked", enumerated over paths, not verbs; a diagnostics verb that samples the mic is still the mic). Remote-triggered recording from a pocket is the same privacy incident with extra steps. ask <text> stays allowed (no mic).

Exit: hold UP+DOWN together 1 s → full refresh → last card restored.

Truth surface: status JSON gains "locked":true|false (spec-mandated field); the glance card shows a lock glyph. ACCEPTANCE (needs D-UX0 + a lock/unlock test verb or Settings toggle): lock → press ai hold must NOT record (no upload event, log line names the refusal) → tap anywhere discarded → status.locked true → unlock chord → status.locked false and touch live again.

docs.title: 12. Glance card — wake-on-lift (P-4)
docs.text:
The 80% interaction of a pocket device: pull it out, look, put it back. Target: glanceable in under 2 s from wake trigger.

  • Trigger: IMU lift-to-look signature, or any button short-press
  • Content (one partial refresh, no full flash if the panel already holds a card): time · battery% · wifi glyph · unread count · lock glyph when locked. One line, top of glass, over whatever card was last shown (e-ink keeps it for free).
  • NOT a page: it draws over the status strip zone and expires from the nav model — BACK/scroll/tap all act on the underlying card.
  • ACCEPTANCE: from sleep, button-press → glance strip visible < 2 s (measured by log timestamps wake→refresh-complete); from awake, strip updates by partial refresh only (no full-panel flash receipt).

docs.title: 13. Sound rules — ratified (M-A6)
docs.text:
The buzzer (GPIO48, LEDC PWM) is the device's fastest output — sound lands ~10× before any pixel (§0). These rules are LAW for every current chime and the coming RTTTL engine.

Sound tiers — every sound the device can make belongs to exactly one:

tier what examples governed by L — local UI feedback consequence of the owner's own touch/button tap blip, ack, dead-end double blip, error Snooze mutes; LOCKED mutes (see below); ≤ 400 ms N — notifications device-initiated, tells a pocketed owner something arrived dm motif, thinker-result chime, low-battery Snooze mutes; LOCKED allows (a notification while pocketed is the product working, §11); ≤ 400 ms O — owner's hand explicitly commanded over the relay play <rtttl>, say with chime NOTHING mutes it — the owner pressing play IS consent; 64-note cap B — boot jingle once per cold boot 4-note motif (M-A6c beat-sync gate) the one exception to 400 ms; Snooze-forever suppresses it

Ratified reconciliation of M-A6 "silent while pocket-locked" vs §11 "chirps still allowed": both were right about different tiers. LOCKED kills tier L trivially (locked discards the inputs that would cause feedback) and keeps tier N — a pocket device that can't chirp an arrival is a brick with better battery life. The owner's public-silence need is served by Snooze (§7 first row), which is a deliberate one-tap act, not a side effect of pocketing. WHY this split: lockout guards inputs (privacy), snooze guards outputs (courtesy) — collapsing them makes one need destroy the other.

Motif taste guide (leitmotif, not alarm): ack = rising major third; error = falling minor second; dm = 4-note motif; dead-end = the double blip, unchanged — it is vocabulary (§0), not music. All motifs live in the B4–C7 resonance sweet spot; envelope via LEDC fade (30 ms attack / 80 ms decay) so chimes ring instead of buzz. WHY leitmotifs: a sound the owner can name without looking replaces a screen glance — that is the entire budget argument for a buzzer on a 2 Hz panel.

Refusals are honest: a tune over 64 notes is refused naming its byte count; play while snoozed still plays (tier O) and the reply says so.

docs.title: 14. Animation usage rules (M-A6b — when may pixels move?)
docs.text:
Physics: ~2 Hz ceiling, ghosting after ~20 open-loop partials (§0). An animation is therefore a budgeted act, never decoration.

  • Closed-loop anims ("closed":true — every pixel returns to its origin state each cycle: blink, invert-pulse, two-phase breathe) accumulate ~zero ghosting because displacement cancels; the player skips wipe_every. These are the ONLY anims allowed to run indefinitely (idle home creature, thinking pulse). WHY: an idle screen that slowly turns grey teaches the owner the device is broken.
  • Open-loop anims (travel, trails, typers) keep the wipe law (wipe_every mandatory) and must be event-bound: they play because something happened (boot, answer arriving, ota progress) and they END — no open-loop anim outlives its event.
  • Dirty-bbox is a cost dial: compact motion (~120 px box) sustains ~3 fps; full-width partials cap at ~2 fps. stickyOS anims are creatures and glyphs, not scene changes — a scene change is a page turn and gets a full refresh.
  • Streaming answers own the panel: no concurrent anim while the typer runs (G6 already defers touch; pixels defer too). One moving thing at a time — the eye on e-ink can't arbitrate two.
  • Beat-sync (M-A6c) inherits its anim's class: a closed-loop 2-frame pulse synced to a jingle is the sanctioned WOW; sound carries the liveliness the panel cannot (§0). Locked/snoozed states strip the tune per §13 and the anim plays silent.

docs.title: 15. Chat — the conversation surface (M-A1/M-S5 successor spec)
docs.text:
Two different things wear bubbles; the spec refuses to blur them: - Ask thread — owner ⇄ their own agent, born from Speak/Type/ask. Ephemeral by default; §7 Agent ▸ ask-history toggles local persistence. - DM thread — owner ⇄ another tiny.technology user (Chats ▸ m:inbox). Server truth; the device is a viewport, never the store. WHY: an agent answer and a human message carry different obligations — a human's words must never be summarized, aged out, or restyled by the device.

Ask lifecycle (one law, five moments): 1. Receipt — the question becomes the user bubble before any network round-trip (shipped: stream_render seeds s_stream_q). A question the glass didn't echo is a question the owner can't trust was heard. 2. Thinking — caret alone, no empty assistant bubble (shipped). The caret is the only legal "spinner" on this hardware. 3. Streaming — G6 rules: stream owns the display, auto-scroll owns the tail, physical long-press-AI is the one exit. 4. Settle — stream end = ONE full refresh (ghost purge + caret removal, shipped) AND the moment tap regions return. Touch bar on a settled ask card: [Speak] [Type] [Home] — a settled answer is an invitation to follow up, in place. 5. Follow-up — Speak/Type from a settled ask card appends to the SAME visual thread (new user bubble below), and the ask request carries the prior turns of THIS thread as context (bounded: last 4 turns or 2KB, oldest dropped first). WHY: "what about in celsius?" must work; an amnesiac chat page is a text card in costume. DEPENDENCY: if /api/devices/ask cannot accept a context array today, firmware ships the visual thread first and the context field is filed in QUESTIONS.md — the UI contract must not wait on the backend.

Thread typography at settle (extends §6): - Newest turn is the tail; entering a thread lands scrolled to the TAIL, not the top (a conversation's present tense is its bottom line). - Older turns scroll away under M12 rules; the scrollbar is the only history indicator. No timestamps inside bubbles — relative time lives in the inbox list row only. WHY: on 4-gray every bubble byte competes with the answer. - An ask that arrives while a DIFFERENT card is showing (relay ask) still takes the panel — asks are owner-initiated by definition, never a surprise.

Inbox (DMs) rules: rows = sender + relative time + first line (fold rules §6); unread = Black dot, read = none — binary, no counts per row (the §12 glance strip owns the aggregate). Opening a thread marks read server-side (shipped semantics); the device never marks read on glance-strip evidence alone. Reply from a DM thread uses the keyboard; cancel returns to the SAME thread unsent (shipped, tiny_shell.cpp:426). DM send is the one action on this device that reaches another human: the composer's OK label reads "Send" on DM threads, never "ok". WHY: the label is the last consent gate.

docs.title: Cards — the render_ui spec (as shipped)
docs.text:
The card renderer (tiny_display.cpp) turns a JSON spec into the 800×480 4-gray panel. It is the view layer for everything: relay render_ui envelopes, stickyOS pages, agent answers, the provisioning screen. Design rule inherited from tiny's render_ui: no code ships in a card — only data; the firmware renders each type natively.

Common fields on every card: title (heading), card_id (echoed by render_ui replies and page — the panel's commit receipt), footer (small line at the bottom), buttons (touch bar, below).

docs.title: text
docs.text:
{"type":"text","title":"Dinner","body":"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge"}
Word-wrapped body. Unknown card types degrade to a labelled error card — never a blank panel.

Check 23's torture card filed two renderer findings; both were root-caused and fixed in 0.14.18 (on glass — this loop sent an id-less card and got card_id=auto-27b6c5df back). A spec without id no longer commits an anonymous card — the firmware synthesizes a stable identity (FNV-1a over type+title, rendered auto-xxxxxxxx), so the same card always gets the same id, the mirror can still correlate, and ui_tap never again reports an empty card_id (the sender gets a log warning so the habit dies too). And the orientation-collage had a real mechanism, not a missing wipe call: partial refresh is a comparison against the last pushed frame — after a rotation that baseline is a differently-oriented picture, so "unchanged" pixels survive as fragments. The fix tracks the rotation of the last pushed frame (s_pushed_rot, updated only on refresh success); any rotation delta forces the full mono wipe past every fast path. The last sibling finding — draw_wrapped's 1024-byte fold buffer cutting long bodies silently at render while scroll exists precisely to browse them — is dead in 0.14.20 (in tree): the fold buffer grows on demand (2× input — the worst real fold expansion is 1.5×, e.g. ©→(c) — under a 16 KB ceiling so a hostile serial write can't OOM the render task). Past the ceiling the text ends in " [cut]" on the glass, never silently; an alloc failure renders "(no memory for text)" — the honest-void idiom again. The dashboard already compensates with a fold-budget pre-flight: a composer lint plus a server-side render_warning, warn-never-refuse (the glass still renders the first 1024 bytes honestly). The estimator mirrors ascii_fold's growth table (✓→[ok], ½→1/2, ß→2 bytes…) and applies it per field, exactly like draw_wrapped's per-call buffer — body, each list item, each composite part, recursively.
