docs.title: qr
docs.text:
{"type":"qr","text":"WIFI:S:tiny-1a2b;T:WPA;P:tinysetup;;","caption":"scan to join"}
Exists because typing an SSID/password off a 4-gray panel is the worst part of setup — the provisioning portal hands your phone a scannable WIFI: code instead. Modules are painted one fill_rect per dark module. Two honesty rules, because an unscannable QR looks exactly like a scannable one from across the room:

  • below 3 px/module a phone camera gives up on e-ink — instead of painting a decorative square, the card says how much room the symbol needed
  • text over the version cap → the card names the byte count that would not encode

(Capped at 12 px/module — no point wasting the panel on a huge symbol.)

docs.title: keyboard (stickyOS)
docs.text: On-e-ink keyboard used by the Wi-Fi join flow — rows of touch keys (shift, bksp, space, cancel, ok) editing a masked value line. Also reachable via render_ui for custom prompts; key taps route to the shell (tiny_shell_key). Long input tail-clips (0.14.5): the value line stays right-anchored so the newest characters are always visible, a ~ marks the cut, and the caret is clamped in-box — typing past ~26 chars portrait / ~46 landscape no longer overdraws.

docs.title: menu (stickyOS)
docs.text: Tappable rows with an optional right-aligned note (e.g. Wi-Fi scan results with RSSI). Row taps route to the shell (tiny_shell_menu). Shows up to 24 items; rows scrolled out of the window are unstaged — an invisible button must not be tappable.

docs.title: Body overflow — scrolling (0.14.x)
docs.text: A text/list/kv/menu body taller than the body box scrolls: the canvas measures full content height through its y-clip, a right-edge track+thumb scrollbar shows position, and steps draw with partial refresh. Fingers scroll by vertical swipe (rotation-aware) or UP/DOWN; agents use the scroll verb, whose reply carries the whole model (offset/content_h/view_h). A card that fits doesn't scroll and says so (scrollable:false).

docs.title: priority (0.14.4 — parsed now, semantics reserved)
docs.text: Any card may declare "priority":"alert" (default "normal"). Today the whole behavior is a visible receipt — the title gains a ! prefix — parsed now so senders can start declaring intent and no future firmware breaks them; the real focus/queue semantics arrive with the notification model. Probed live on 0.14.4 glass.

docs.title: chart (0.14.16)
docs.text:
{"type":"chart","title":"Battery","data":[92,90,88,85,84],"style":"line","y_min":0,"y_max":100}
Sparkline-class line/bar renderer — battery and temperature history finally have somewhere to draw. Auto-scales unless y_min/y_max pin the range, and the scale values are drawn on the axis — a chart that hides its scale is a mood, not a measurement. E-ink-tuned choices: 2 px stroke (1 px ghosts on this panel), dotted midline, first/last x-labels only (more would collide), 160-point cap. Honest-void rather than a fake plot on <2 points or when a composite squeezes it below 60 px. Additive — grammar v2 stands.

docs.title: buttons
docs.text:
Not a body — a touch bar: up to 4 buttons drawn at the bottom (56 px bar, 24 px margins, 16 px gaps, width split evenly), attachable to any card: 

{"type":"text","title":"Dinner","body":"Pizza in fridge",
 "buttons":[{"id":"done","label":"Done"},{"id":"later","label":"Later"}]}
A tap on a button the shell doesn't own goes upstream as a ui_tap device note → the owner's activity feed → the agent answers with the next card. The screen is a conversation.

docs.title: chat (since 0.15.2, grammar v3 — STREAMING_UI.md)
docs.text:
The iOS conversation, translated to 4-gray: user messages are LightGray-filled rounded bubbles on the right, assistant messages are outlined white bubbles on the left (radius 12, max-width the spec-exact 70% of the lane since 0.16.8/R-3 — designer-verified off a panel PNG in verdict batch #8: a long assistant bubble measured 508 px of the 752 px body lane, 67.6%, under the 526 px cap; a single short line shrinks to its own width — "Yes." is a chip, not a banner). Scrollable like every long body. 

{"type":"chat","card_id":"ask","messages":[
  {"role":"user","body":"what's the weather"},
  {"role":"assistant","body":"Sunny, 24C."}
]}
A streamed text ask renders as this card automatically: the question echoes as the user bubble (the receipt), and the answer types into the assistant bubble at ≤2 Hz partial refresh with a caret at the tail, then settles with one full refresh. Voice asks keep the plain text card — the device never sees its own transcript and must not invent an echo.

docs.title: Planned (not yet dispatched)
docs.text: image/stream (pre-dithered frame blit — the 1-bit blit path blit_1bit already exists in the renderer). Until then the qr, kv, chart and composite types cover the practical cases.

docs.title: Refresh policy (e-ink physics, honestly)
docs.text:
what mode speed text / list / kv / menu / keyboard / buttons monochrome full ~600 ms class status-bar clock, scroll steps, frame sequences partial fastest, some ghosting photo-grade cards (gray4:true) 4-level full slowest, prettiest

Minimum 1.5 s between refreshes; bursts coalesce (queue, render last). A goodbye card survives deep sleep at 0 mA — e-ink keeps the image with every rail off.

docs.title: Commands — the envelope verb reference
docs.text:
Everything the Sticky answers to, exactly as tiny_node.cpp dispatches it — last audited against the tree at 0.16.6-m14, grammar v4 (the homepage pins what's verified on the glass, which may trail the tree by a version). Envelopes arrive as {type:"invoke", prompt:"<verb> [args]"} over the relay; every verb replies (unknown input answers the help string — never silence). These are also the capabilities the heartbeat advertises, and the rule is: advertise only what dispatch actually implements.

Send from any tiny surface:

use_device invoke → prompt: "status"

docs.title: render_ui <card-json>
docs.text:
Renders a card spec on the e-ink. Replies rendered card_id=<id> — the id the panel actually committed, so a mirror can claim "this IS what is on the glass" rather than "the last card I sent".

render_ui {"type":"text","title":"Dinner","body":"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge"}

docs.title: say <text>
docs.text: Put words on the fridge — no agent turn, no network wait. Renders a text card titled tiny (card_id=say) and plays the ack chime. Replies said (card on the panel).

docs.title: screenshot
docs.text: Framebuffer → hosted PNG → replies screenshot: https://plugin.tiny.technology/media/…. This is render ground truth — the agent (and the dashboard mirror) see the actual panel, not a belief about it.

docs.title: page home|status|sensors|settings|wifi|ble|back|next|prev
docs.text: The relay twin of every tappable navigation path in stickyOS (the M10 parity rule: anything a finger can do, an envelope can do). Replies page <arg> -> ESP_OK (card_id=…).

docs.title: rotate [0|90|180|270|auto]
docs.text:
The UI follows the body. Bare rotate reports; a degree value sets the layout rotation and holds it (manual mode — a human's choice outranks gravity); rotate auto hands the decision back to the accelerometer.

{"rotation":90, "mode":"manual", "imu_last":"portrait-right", "imu_last_deg":90,
 "result":"ESP_OK", "summary":"rotation 90 deg (manual), imu says portrait-right"}

Auto-rotate policy (deliberately small): commit only after several consecutive identical IMU readings — a ~600 ms visible e-ink refresh must never chase a wobble; flat on a table (flat) says nothing about which edge is up, so the last standing orientation wins. Coordinate invariant: the layout turns; the framebuffer, screenshot and touch coordinates stay in panel space — a tap aimed at a screenshot pixel still lands.

docs.title: tap <x> <y>
docs.text:
A synthetic tap in panel coordinates — the screenshot's own coordinate system — through the same resolver a finger uses. This is how a rotation gets proven without a human hand: tap where the screenshot shows the button, and see which button answers.

{"tap":[400,440], "rotation":90, "result":"ESP_OK", "card_id":"home",
 "summary":"tapped 400,440 at 90 deg -> ESP_OK"}

Together, screenshot → tap → screenshot closes the loop the agent needs to test the UI end-to-end with no one in the room.

docs.title: swipe <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> (since 0.16.2, grammar v4)
docs.text:
A synthetic swipe in panel coordinates, driven through the same release classifier a finger uses — so what it proves is the real gesture grammar, not a parallel code path. This is how UX_SPEC §2 rules get verified over the relay: inject the vector, read the receipt, screenshot the consequence.

// receipt shape since 0.16.6 (route-time, two stages named);
// "route" added in 0.16.7 (R-6b, tap and swipe both):
{"swipe":[400,60,400,300], "rotation":90,
 "accepted":"ESP_OK",          // classifier verdict at inject
 "routed":true,                // the route actually FINISHED before this reply
 "route":"ESP_OK",             // the route's OWN verdict (0.16.7, verified on
                               // glass): any esp_err name — ESP_OK = nav
                               // happened, ESP_ERR_NOT_ALLOWED = announced
                               // dead-end, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE = scroll with
                               // nothing to scroll (content fits), "none" = no
                               // route ran — before this field a dead-end and
                               // a nav returned identical receipts
 "card_id":"home",             // display-time, no longer inject-time
 "summary":"... -> ESP_OK, route completed; card_id is display-time"}

The summary's third clause is one of: refused at classifier · route completed · route still running at reply time (slow render — probe again, not lost) · no route dispatched (accepted but a dead-end gesture).

INVALID_SIZE means the travel stayed within the 24 px tap slop — refused rather than silently downgraded to a tap, because a probe that quietly becomes a different gesture proves nothing. Buttons and long-press still have no synthetic twin (press is not a verb yet), so those stay hand-verified.

Probe under rotation: coordinates are panel space but the gesture is classified in logical space — under rotation:90 a panel-horizontal swipe is logically vertical and routes to scroll, not page-turn (live probe on 0.16.7: the same 200,240 → 500,240 vector answered route:ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE — scroll with nothing to scroll — at 90°, and popped a pushed card at 0°). Read the receipt's rotation field before interpreting route, or pin the frame with rotate 0 first.

History worth keeping: verdict batch #5 convicted the first receipt design using this verb — R-5 (a 40 px sub-slop swipe answered ESP_OK) and R-6 (card_id written at inject time raced the async route, same torn-read family as the M9 draw-time-regions lesson). Both fixed and VERIFIED ON GLASS at 0.16.6-m14 (6af1449, fw_commit 47821b73): the receipt waits for the route to finish and reports display-time state, with the accepted/routed stages separated so an accepted-but-dead-end gesture can no longer masquerade as success. Live probes against the panel: a bottom-band swipe answered "accepted":"ESP_OK","routed":true,"card_id":"home" with the card provably home, and a 20 px probe was ESP_ERR_INVALID_SIZE, refused at classifier. One correction to the record: R-5's original probe used 40 px of travel and called it "sub-slop" — but kTapSlop is 24 px (tiny_touch.cpp), so 40 px was always a legitimate swipe and its ESP_OK was correct; the receipt design (inject-time, R-6) was the real defect, and it is gone. On a device still running ≤0.16.5, let a follow-up status/screenshot — not the swipe reply — prove the consequence. tap got the same route-time contract (12 s wait, because a tap can trigger a blocking route like the ~8 s BLE scan; "routed":false means still running, not lost).

Advertising gap — CLOSED in 0.16.8. From 0.16.4 to 0.16.7, swipe was dispatched but missing from the heartbeat's capabilities array, so the fleet's device list under-reported the surface. Fixed in 4dd7fcf and verified end-to-end on 0.16.8: use_device list now shows all 16 verbs, swipe included. The rule stands — advertise exactly what dispatch implements — and this section keeps the incident because under-advertising is the quiet failure mode of that rule.

docs.title: scroll [up|down|top|<±px>]
docs.text:
Moves an overflowing card body (text/list/kv/menu taller than the body box). Bare scroll just reports — the probe form; up/down step ⅔ of a view (the buttons' relay twin), top rewinds, a signed pixel count is probe-precise. Always clamped at the edges; on a card that fits, scrollable comes back false and nothing moves. A right-edge track+thumb scrollbar shows position on the glass; steps draw with partial refresh.

{"offset":474, "content_h":1012, "view_h":356, "scrollable":true,
 "card_id":"scrolltest", "result":"ESP_OK",
 "summary":"scroll 474/656 px of 1012 content (ESP_OK)"}

The reply carries the whole scroll model (offset / content_h / view_h), so scrolling is provable without a finger — the same probe-readable discipline as rotate and tap. Quirk (0.14.4): scroll 0 is indistinguishable from the bare report form (atoi returns 0 for both) — to go to the top, say scroll top, never scroll 0; the dashboard works around this the same way. (This verb also has a war story: its first landing was eaten by a shared-tree race and shipped as an advertised-but-unknown command — the incident behind the build-discipline rules.)

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Since 0.14.10 the reply carries fw_commit: a build-time-injected git sha with a --dirty suffix for uncommitted trees, so the version string can prove ancestry instead of asserting it (generated at build time, not configure time — stale-sha-on-incremental is the exact collision class retired). One caveat, stated when it shipped: on a shared worktree -dirty names the checkout's state, not necessarily the firmware's. Machine-readable JSON — the dashboard parses fields directly; a summary field inside carries the human sentence, so one verb serves both readers instead of two that can disagree.

Fields: fw, grammar_version, device_id, battery_pct, charging, wifi, ssid, rssi_dbm, heap_free, psram_free, uptime, summary. Provenance honesty: a gauge that didn't answer yields null, never false — "not charging" is a claim.

grammar_version (0.14.4) is the field consumers should gate on: the verb grammar is a 3-consumer contract (dashboard, iOS StickyPanel, relay agents) and this integer bumps on any change to a verb, its arguments, or a reply shape. It exists because a version string is data inside the image and can lie about content — proven the night an uncommitted build shipped as "0.14.2" advertising a verb it didn't dispatch. v1 = the 14-verb grammar of 0.14.3; v2 (0.14.11) = the messages dialect — the messages verb family plus the m: button-id namespace (inbox / thread / compose).

docs.title: sensors [card]
docs.text:
Every onboard sensor, read live over I²C1 — no network either way. Bare verb replies JSON; sensors card also paints the sensors page on the glass. Since 0.14.11 the BQ27220's mAh fields carry their own provenance: the gauge had reported full_charge_mah: 7500 on a 750 mAh pack since first read — off by exactly 10× — and the brief carried it as a known-lying field for two days. The fix reads DesignCapacity (standard command 0x3C) and adds design_mah + pack_mah + mah_trusted (field names measured off the live wire, not predicted — an earlier draft of this line said design_capacity_mah, which the firmware never emitted), so the absolute-mAh fields now say whether to believe them instead of asking the reader to know the datasheet.

🩹 A bug that lived on the wire for three builds (fixed + wire-verified on 0.14.14): the provenance fields pushed the reply past its buffer and a strlcpy whose return value was discarded truncated it silently — sensors shipped JSON cut mid-token at byte 767 while claiming ESP_OK, measured twice byte-identical. Two lessons survived the fix. The builder's own probe showed the cut and it was misread as sed clipping the line — a truncated receipt is itself evidence, not noise in the pipeline that carried it. And the dashboard's answer was defense-in-depth: a salvage parser (bracket/string-state scan, unit-tested against the actual truncated wire capture) plus a truncation banner — recover what's intact, confess what isn't. This loop re-measured on 0.14.14: complete reply, parses clean, errors[] and all — the published receipt agrees (767 B invalid → 840 B valid). And the defect was then treated as a class, not an instance: 0.14.16 (verified on glass — this loop's probe and an independent check both parsed clean) kills the same silent truncation on status and messages unread before it fires, and a follow-up audit swept every remaining fixed buffer on the reply paths. DesignCapacity measured at 7500 on the 750 mAh pack — and the fix was deliberately not a blind ÷10: if the gauge's CC-Gain is also off by 10× the errors cancel and today's working percentage would break, so mah_trusted:false stands (with an errors[] confession in the JSON) until a 30-second unplug test — owner's hands required — decides which of two opposite fixes applies.

{
  "temperature_c": 24.1, "humidity_pct": 41.2,          // SHT40
  "orientation": "flat", "accel": {"x":…}, "gyro": {…}, // LSM6DS3TR-C (gyro power-cycled per read, ~110 ms)
  "rtc": "2026-08-25T21:04:11Z", "rtc_zone": "UTC",
  "clock_source": "sntp",                                // sntp | rtc | none — the field is honest about provenance
  "battery": { "percent":…, "voltage_mv":…, "current_ma":…, "remaining_mah":…,
               "full_charge_mah":…, "health_pct":…, "cycle_count":…,
               "temperature_c":…, "charging":…, "full":…, "present":…,
               "design_mah":…, "pack_mah":…, "mah_trusted":… }  // BQ27220
}

Read mah_trusted before you believe any mAh field (0.14.18-m12). design_mah is what the gauge says the pack is (DesignCapacity 0x3C, measured on this device: 7500); pack_mah is the nameplate (750, docs/hardware.md). They disagree by 10x, so mah_trusted is false and errors[] carries bq27220: design 7500 mAh vs 750 mAh pack - mAh untrusted. design_mah:0 means the read failed. percent comes straight from the gauge register StateOfCharge (0x2C) and is NOT computed from these fields — but see the JOURNAL entry for why a 10x design capacity can still bend the percentage in the middle of a discharge even while it is right at both ends. The three keys are additive; nothing in the dashboard consumed the mAh fields.

docs.title: miccheck [seconds] (1–10 s, default 2)
docs.text:
Records PDM audio and replies RMS/peak instead of uploading: {"verdict":"live|SILENT","rms":…,"peak":…,"nonzero_pct":…,"samples":…,"secs":…}. A dead post-wake mic mux reads flat zeros; a live mic reads the room's noise floor — this is how sleep → wake → mic gets proven with nobody home to speak.

The device has exactly three microphone paths

voice, ask-via-AI-button, and miccheck — and a pocket device must be able to gate all three at once. 0.17.0's lockout gates two of them — and the D-UX5 ruling ("guard the audio entry point, not a list of verb names") turned out to be prophecy, not caution: the shipped gate is a verb-name check on voice, and the docs lane's on-glass probe showed a locked device still answers miccheck with live room audio. miccheck never uploads, but it is still a microphone. Details in the lock/unlock bug box; filed P1.

docs.title: ask <text>
docs.text: Owner-scoped agent turn via POST /api/devices/ask → {text, card?} — the answer paints as a card. Since 0.15.0 the ask streams (STREAMING_UI.md): the request carries stream:"1", and a backend that knows the flag answers SSE — the words type onto the glass live (chat card: question = user bubble, answer types into the assistant bubble, caret at the tail, closing full refresh), and the relay reply text gains a [streamed to glass] suffix. A backend that ignores the flag gets the classic render-once path — the flag is an opt-in the server may decline. One ask at a time across all callers (button + relay share a single-flight mutex); a second concurrent ask is refused, never queued. This is the full agent, not a Q&A endpoint: tools, memory, cross-device reach — proven on glass with "what is my Mac mini's current disk usage?" answered from the wall (the turn ran use_device against another machine in the fleet). A 422 means nothing transcribed / empty speech; the firmware paints an honest "didn't catch that" card instead of pretending.

docs.title: voice [seconds] (default 5)
docs.text: Same pipeline, but records the PDM mic first: WAV → /api/media → ask with audioUrl. This is exactly what the AI button does — the verb exists so the pipeline is testable remotely.

docs.title: lock / unlock (since 0.17.0, grammar v5)
docs.text:
Pocket lockout — the P-1 safety pillar, manual half (IMU auto-entry is the next package). status carries the truth as "locked". While locked: physical touch is discarded at the router, AI press answers a double blip through the fabric and refuses, long-press home and UP/DOWN paging are dead, and the relay voice verb refuses — a remote-triggered pocket recording is the same privacy incident as an accidental one. The relay otherwise stays answerable by design: say/render_ui/screenshot/tap all work, because lockout guards the device's inputs, not the owner's reach (synthetic taps bypass the router gate on purpose). The unlock chord — UP+DOWN held 1 s — is read as raw GPIO by its own watcher task, deliberately independent of the button layer it gates: the one path back cannot be disabled by the thing it escapes. Unlock re-renders the last card; lockout is a state, not a page.

Verified hole (P1) — found on glass, fixed in tree, receipt pending

The docs lane ran the D-UX5 probe on the live 0.17.0 panel: a locked device answered miccheck 2 with two seconds of room audio (rms 2188, peak 11605, 99% nonzero). The gate was a verb-name check on voice; the audio entry point was unguarded — exactly the failure mode D-UX5 pre-registered before the build. Mitigation: miccheck never uploads (only RMS numbers leave the device). 0.17.1 (in tree) fixes it at the exact spot the ruling named — tiny_audio_record_wav, the single funnel every capture path passes through (voice verb, AI button, miccheck, and any future caller), refusing with ESP_ERR_NOT_ALLOWED while locked. Found-on-glass bugs get closed on glass: this box stays until a locked miccheck returns a refusal on the physical panel.

One more truth from the incident: the "locked at boot" sighting was a queued probe envelope, not boot state — the device boots unlocked (receipt-logged in 0.17.1). Which means a pocket reboot (crash, brownout) silently exits lockout; noted here as an open edge for the IMU auto-entry package, which would re-enter on its own.

docs.title: sleep [seconds]
docs.text: Deep sleep. Order matters, and it's deliberate: reply first (the PATCH must land while the radio is up) → paint the goodbye card (e-ink keeps it at 0 mA — that is the magic) → hand over to the HAL, which holds the power latch and gates the wake pin. The AI button (EXT1, GPIO4) always wakes; optional seconds adds a timer wake so sleep is remotely testable.

docs.title: messages [unread | thread <login>] (since 0.14.7)
docs.text: The DM rail, driven remotely. Bare messages puts the inbox card on the glass; messages thread <login> opens that conversation; messages unread answers the badge counts as JSON and renders nothing (a monitoring probe should not repaint a panel). All three fetch with the device's own token over /api/devices/messages — no owner-side process anywhere. Same paths as a finger: a tapped m: row and a pushed verb converge on one fetch-and-render.

docs.title: ota [channel] (default sticky-dev)
docs.text: Stage from the channel pointer → sha256-verify → reply then reboot into a rollback-armed trial (after esp_restart nobody would hear the result). Replies already up to date (<fw version>) when current, OTA failed: <esp_err> otherwise. Since 0.14.9 the stage also refuses downgrades: ver_cmp parses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-mN] numerically (0.2.0 < 0.14.8 — no lexicographic trap), an unparseable version is INCOMPARABLE, and incomparable-without-force = refuse, fail closed. The refusal reply is an actionable sentence, not an error code. A publisher who truly means to go backwards writes force:"1" into the bundle — and the forced install logs loudly.

docs.title: Not in the firmware (yet)
docs.text: wake (a sleeping device can only be woken by button/timer — the radio is off), reprovision (the rescue portal opens itself after a 3-strike auth-halt — 0.14.12), press (no synthetic twin for buttons/long-press yet — tap and swipe cover the touchscreen but not the three physical keys), image/stream (planned; the qr card and render_ui cover most needs today). ~~lock/unlock~~ shipped in 0.17.0 and moved up to Power & lifecycle — the pre-registered probe (tools/probe_lockout.sh) did its job both ways: the build had a test to meet, and the test caught the one gate the build missed (miccheck, see the bug box there). The dashboard greys these out with the reason — an action that does nothing is a lie on the screen.

docs.title: Reply plumbing (all verbs)
docs.text: Replies go PATCH /api/devices/relay with inReplyTo and a payload that is a JSON-serialized string ({"result":"…"}), capped at 8 KB; images ride as hosted URLs, never bytes. A single 401 never wipes identity (blips happen — the M9 lesson, learned when one transient 401 bricked a good token): three consecutive auth failures trip an auth-halt (auth_halted:true in status), and since 0.14.12 the halt raises a rescue portal — live STA widens to APSTA, the same /setup contract as first boot, so a re-issued token has a path onto the device without a serial cable. STA stays associated throughout, so a 401 that clears self-heals without the portal ever being used.

docs.title: Compose for the glass — a cookbook
docs.text: Recipes for putting things on the Sticky's e-ink from an agent. Everything here was checked against dispatch() and the card renderers at the commit this page last changed — anything the firmware doesn't do yet is marked planned, not implied.

docs.title: Four ways in
docs.text:
path when how sticky_display tiny-tool you are one of the owner's tinys with ~/.tiny/tools loaded {text:"…"} → say · {card:"<json>"} → render_ui · {verb:"status"} → anything else. Waits ~20 s; a still-pending envelope is returned honestly with its id use_device any tiny surface (iOS, web, another machine) action:'invoke', device sticky, prompt = the verb string itself, e.g. say hello or render_ui {...} dashboard a human at a browser buttons light from the device's advertised caps; unsupported actions are greyed with the reason raw relay HTTP no tiny runtime at all POST /api/devices/relay {toDevice, payload:{type:'invoke', prompt}} with an owner Bearer → poll GET /api/devices/relay?inReplyTo=<id>. Replies are a JSON-serialized string, ≤ 8 KB — see Commands → reply plumbing

The device polls its relay every 5 s awake, backing off to 60 s idle — a "slow" first response is usually just the poll cadence, not a fault. Asleep, it answers nothing until a button or timer wakes it (why there is no wake verb).

docs.title: Say something (the one-liner)
docs.text:
say Kettle's boiled — tea window: 4 minutes

Plain text, monochrome full refresh, on the glass in one panel cycle. With the tiny-tool, {text, title} upgrades this to a titled text card.

docs.title: A glanceable status card
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"kv","id":"brew","title":"Kombucha — day 6",
  "rows":[["pH","3.4"],["temp","24.1 C"],["started","Aug 20"],["bottle","in 2 days"]],
  "footer":"sensors read 03:20Z"}

kv is the workhorse for agent status. Put provenance in the footer — the panel persists for hours, so when the data was true matters more than on a phone (the glance cluster carries the same discipline).

docs.title: A tappable menu — the screen answers back
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"menu","id":"lunch","title":"Lunch?",
  "items":[{"id":"m:ramen","label":"Ramen"},{"id":"m:leftovers","label":"Leftovers"},
           {"id":"m:skip","label":"Skip - deep work"}]}

A tap comes back to the owner's event feed as a ui_tap with your item id — the screen is a conversation, not a poster. Design ids like the firmware's own namespaces (m:t:<login> in the messages app): the destination travels in the id, so no state needs remembering. Menus show up to 24 items and unstage off-window rows — an invisible button is never tappable.

docs.title: A chart that admits its scale
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"chart","id":"temp24h","title":"Office temp - 24h",
  "series":[21.2,21.4,22.8,24.1,23.6,22.2,21.9],"unit":"C"}

Axis labels are drawn because a chart that hides its scale is a mood, not a measurement; under 2 points or a 60 px squeeze it renders an honest void (cards → chart).

docs.title: A QR that hands off to a phone
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"qr","id":"handoff","title":"Full report",
  "data":"https://tiny.technology/s/abc123","caption":"scan for the long version"}

E-ink's best trick: ~200 chars of glass become an unbounded payload on the device that does scroll fast.

docs.title: Probe the UI with no one in the room
docs.text:
screenshot            → hosted PNG of the real framebuffer
tap 400 440           → same resolver a finger uses; receipt names the button
swipe 400 60 400 300  → same release classifier; INVALID_SIZE = within tap slop
screenshot            → prove the consequence

The verified loop for testing what you rendered — tap / swipe. One honesty rule from the P0 postmortem: a receipt is not proof the consequence survived — always close with the second screenshot.

docs.title: Stream an answer (the typer)
docs.text: ask <text> with a streaming-aware backend types the answer onto the glass word by word (~2 Hz — the panel's partial-refresh budget, not a simulation of one). One ask at a time, fleet-wide; a second is refused, never queued. Full design: Streaming UI.

docs.title: What you cannot compose yet
docs.text: wish status anim card (agent-generated frame sequences) planned — M-A directives filed; partial-refresh frame stepping is the mechanism, UX_SPEC §14 is the usage law. Not in the renderer today: render_ui {"type":"anim"…} is refused with the reason image / stream cards (photo on the glass) planned — the 1-bit blit path exists in the renderer; the card types don't. qr + chart + composite cover most needs RTTTL music on the buzzer planned (M-A6) — today the buzzer speaks a 3-word vocabulary: blip (accepted), double-blip (refused), chime. It is a buzzer, not a speaker: chimes yes, speech never video never — physics, not roadmap: the panel's full refresh floors at 1–2 s. The honest ceiling is a slideshow cadence, and the docs will keep calling it that

docs.title: E-ink etiquette (why your card renders "slowly")
docs.text:
• Refreshes floor at 1.5 s apart; bursts coalesce — queue, render last. Design cards to be final, not chatty: one good card beats four updates.
  • A card left on the glass costs 0 mA — e-ink holds the image with every rail off. Lean on that: render, then leave it alone.
  • Full policy: cards → refresh policy.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Seeed reTerminal Sticky — 106 × 65.5 × 7.3 mm, 70 g, IP40, N52 magnets in all four corners. 750 mAh battery. A printable pocket bumper case exists — corner-wrap design that leaves every edge middle open, because no vendor STEP exists and an unverified cutout is a wrong cutout.

MCU ESP32-S3 (QFN56 r0.2), 8 MB PSRAM, 32 MB QSPI flash Display 3.97" 800×480 e-ink, 235 ppi, 4-level gray, SPI (SSD1677-class) Touch GT911 capacitive, I²C0 Sensors SHT40 (temp/RH), LSM6DS3TR-C IMU, PCF8563 RTC, BQ27220 fuel gauge Audio in PDM microphone Audio out magnetic buzzer on PWM USB USB-C, CH343 serial — on cagatay-mac: /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881 SDK ESP-IDF v5.4

docs.title: Pin map
docs.text: Verified against three independent sources: the official hardware-overview docs, the community reterminal-sticky-2048 production source, and — as of this audit — the running firmware's own pin_config.h, which agrees pin-for-pin with everything below and contributed the two power-path pins the other sources omit.

microSD shares SPI2

microSD CS is GPIO8 on the same bus (card power enable GPIO10) — never drive it concurrently with a display transfer. Cards must be FAT32/exFAT with MBR; fonts ship as fonts/*.fpack. Hot-insert is supported.

docs.text:
function GPIO notes AI / Power button 4 deep-sleep EXT1 wake source Up 5 Down 6 Power HOLD 45 must be held HIGH or the device powers off Power LOCK 46 latch pulse low→high→low Battery charge enable 39 EN_BAT_CHGn, active low (firmware source only) PDM mic CLK 19 ⚠ see deep-sleep note PDM mic DATA 20 ⚠ see deep-sleep note Mic power enable 38 TPS22916 load switch Buzzer PWM 48 USB-C serial TX 43 / RX 44 reset = CHIP_PU

Deep-sleep mic deafness (known silicon gotcha)

After a deep-sleep wake, the ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for native USB-Serial-JTAG, muting the PDM mic (every post-sleep capture returns nothing). Fix, applied in tiny_boot before I²S init: clear USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable, gpio_reset_pin(19/20), and clean-cycle the mic rail (GPIO38 low 150 ms).

docs.title: Display refresh modes
docs.text:
The vendor HAL exposes three refresh APIs (with 180° rotation handled in the driver):

mode speed use 4-gray full slowest, prettiest photo-grade cards (gray4:true) monochrome full ~600 ms class text / list / kv / qr / menu / keyboard / buttons cards partial fastest, some ghosting status-bar clock, frame sequences

Firmware policy: minimum 1.5 s between refreshes, bursts coalesced (queue, render last).

docs.title: Honesty notes — what this hardware cannot do
docs.text:
• No speaker. GPIO48 drives a magnetic buzzer via LEDC PWM. Chimes and melodies are first-class; intelligible speech is not achievable — an experiment track for 8-bit PCM-via-PWM exists, measured not promised. Voice input is fully supported (PDM mic → WAV → backend).
  • No video. E-ink full refresh is physically 1–2 s (partial ~300–500 ms with ghosting). "Stream" means sequential frames at time-lapse cadence — perfect for printer progress or a live sensor chart, never for smooth motion.
  • No LAN server. The device is a client — it polls the relay; nothing needs to reach it behind NAT (the provisioning portal is the one exception, and it exists only until Wi-Fi is configured).

docs.title: stickyOS — the local shell (M10)
docs.text: The Sticky is not just a remote-controlled panel: it has a local shell — pages, navigation, a settings app, an on-e-ink keyboard — that works with the network gone. The card renderer is the view layer; pages are local card specs with local tap handlers. Navigation never touches the network — that is the phone feel.

docs.title: The pages
docs.text:
home  →  status  →  sensors  →  settings  →  (ring wraps)
                                   ├─ wifi (scan · join with on-eink keyboard)
                                   └─ bluetooth (scan-only)
page what it shows home app grid (buttons bar): Ask tiny · Status · Sensors · Settings status fw, Wi-Fi/SSID/RSSI, heap, battery — same data as the status verb sensors SHT40, IMU orientation, RTC, battery gauge — live I²C reads, tap Refresh to re-read settings device identity, network, firmware — with a button bar: Wi-Fi · Bluetooth · Back · Home wifi scan results as a tappable menu (RSSI notes, results cached 60 s, Rescan to force) → join flow with the on-e-ink keyboard card (shift/backspace/space/cancel/ok) bluetooth nearby BLE devices (name, address, RSSI) via a NimBLE observer — scan-only honesty: the firmware can see devices, not pair with them, and the page says so instead of implying more

docs.title: Input model
docs.text:
gesture action UP / DOWN buttons the scroll wheel when the card overflows (⅔-view steps, clamped — no fall-through past the edge); cycle the page ring only when the card fits vertical swipe scrolls an overflowing body — rotation-aware and natural-direction, measured in panel coords and resolved against the current orientation horizontal swipe (0.14.17) page turn — left = next, right = prev, on the same page ring the buttons cycle. Classified in logical space (only the display knows which axis is which after rotation), ≥80 px so a sloppy diagonal scroll doesn't flip pages, and a draft outranks a gesture — horizontal over the composer is refused rather than eating unsent words. The ring cycles the four roots only (home → status → sensors → settings); wifi/bluetooth are drill pages a tap opens — since 0.16.5, after the batch-#4 P0 traced to the ring modulus swallowing them (see troubleshooting). On a pushed card the directions split (0.16.7, R-7 — verified on glass by relay probe): mid-content right pops to the parent — phone muscle memory, and a one-thumb target the 48 px left band can't be while walking (P-1); the pop path brings up no radio, so the batch-#4 crash family stays unreachable. Mid-content left stays an announced dead-end (double blip, nothing moves) — "forward" from a drilled place has nowhere to go, and saying so beats pretending. On ≤0.16.6 both directions are the dead-end. Note the pop is to the stack parent — wherever the card was pushed from (a page wifi sent over the relay while on home pops back to home, not to settings) edge-band nav (0.16.4, VERIFIED-ON-GLASS batch #5 on 0.16.5) one spatial rule, no modes — an edge origin marks nav intent (bands are layout-space: last 56 rows, first 48 columns; travel ≥120 px, ≥2× dominant axis). Bottom band + up = HOME from anywhere (on the keyboard = cancel, routed so each composer keeps its own exit: wifi → list, compose → thread, ask → home); left band + right = BACK — pops a pushed card, ring-prev at a ring root. The accept blip fires before the render (on e-ink the ack must be felt before it can be seen); a recognized-but-refused gesture double-blips; below thresholds = silence. During a streaming answer the stream owns the display: every gesture gets one blip and is discarded — the one exit is the physical long-press-AI abort. Verified with screenshots: G1 (settings → bottom-band ↑ → home, 4.6% pixel diff vs home baseline) and G2 (pushed card → left-band → home) both accepted in verdict batch #5 — the same rule that FAILED on 0.16.2 when the verdict ran two images behind the code, which is why the badge waited for receipts instead of trusting the tree AI button, single press ask tiny (voice) AI button, long-press home key — from anywhere turn the device the UI turns with it — IMU auto-rotate commits only after the accelerometer settles (a visible ~600 ms e-ink refresh must never chase a wobble); rotate 0|90|180|270 holds an orientation against gravity, rotate auto releases it. FIXED (63566f0, delivered 0.14.23, owner-confirmed on hardware 2026-08-26 ~02:09Z: "it worked! now the upsite down problem is solved"). It really was a constant 180° in all four orientations — classify() was calibrated off raw-panel axis comments while sticky_display rotates the framebuffer 180° on every push. Do not "fix" the table in tiny_orient.cpp back; the ten-line comment there says why. The follow-on bug is fixed too: rotate report used to set rotation to 0/manual because it fell through to a setter where atoi("report") is 0 (0.15.1, proven on glass) tap page-owned regions handled locally; anything else goes upstream as ui_tap

Navigation is a stack: open() pushes, back pops, the bottom is always home.

Since 0.14.21 (in tree) every title bar carries a right-aligned glance cluster — time, battery, Wi-Fi — where each part earns its place or is omitted: the clock only when SNTP has actually synced, and Z-suffixed until the open timezone question is answered (an unlabeled wrong-zone clock is a lie); battery only when the BQ27220 gauge answers; w+/w- always, because on a pocket device w- is the load-bearing state — it says "answers may be stale." The honest limit is filed with the feature: e-ink persistence means the cluster is only as fresh as the last render — a card left up for an hour shows an hour-old battery. The real periodic status strip stays on the debt list; this ships the glance value without a new refresh cadence to battery-budget.

Overflowing bodies (text/list/kv/menu taller than the body box) scroll with a right-edge track+thumb scrollbar, drawn in partial refresh; a menu shows up to 24 items and unstages off-window rows, because an invisible button must not be tappable. The whole model is probe-readable without a finger via the scroll verb.
