docs.title: The parity rule
docs.text: Every tappable path has a relay twin — page home|status|sensors|settings|wifi|ble|back|next|prev — so the agent (and the dashboard) can walk the same UI a finger can, and each reply carries the resulting card_id as the commit receipt. Nothing is finger-only; nothing is agent-only.

docs.title: Provenance discipline
docs.text:
A recurring theme you'll find in the journal: a field must be right about its own provenance.

  • the clock: RTC→system at boot, SNTP→system→RTC on Wi-Fi-up (a background task keeps waiting off the boot path, 20×15 s, so a slow first exchange still ends at clock_source:"sntp"); UTC by convention
  • the gyro is really read (powered up ~110 ms, sampled, powered down) — not a cached zero
  • a gauge that didn't answer reports null, never false — "not charging" is a claim
  • every new card layout gets screenshotted on real glass before its gate closes

docs.title: Messages on the glass
docs.text:
The owner's tiny.technology DMs render on the panel: an inbox (threads + unread counts), thread views, and notification pushes. Since 0.14.7 the messages app lives in firmware: tap the inbox, and the device fetches with its own token over /api/devices/messages, parses, and paints — no owner-side process in the loop. The footer states its evidence: "4 conversations - 2 unread - tap a row". A thread opens on the newest message — measured, not asserted: the scroll receipt reads offset 576/576, and the footer says "newest 6 loaded - swipe".

Since 0.14.11 the glass also composes: a thread's reply button (m:c:<login> — pure UI, no network) hands off to the e-ink keyboard, and its ok sends with the device token, then re-opens the thread — the reply appearing in the conversation IS the receipt, no separate toast. Failure paints an honest send failed card, because a swallowed 4xx after typing on e-ink at 2 keys/sec is the cruelest possible bug. One boundary still held: the first real send goes to a recipient the owner names, not a test string to a real person — a surface that can speak as you enters service by decision, not by default.

The mechanism is deliberately stateless: a thread row's button id is its destination (m:t:<login>, inbox is m:inbox) — the destination travels in the id, so no card needs to remember what is on the glass. Which is why 0.14.17's sweep fix matters here more than anywhere: a clipped login is not a truncated string, it is a wrong recipient. Three id producers had never been sized to the 48-byte contract they feed; all are now sized and checked, and on overflow the affordance is omitted or refused — no [Reply] button beats one aimed at the wrong human, and a send receipt that would show somebody else's thread stays missing while the send itself still returns its honest ESP_OK. A sibling of that principle shipped in 0.14.20's HEAD repair: a char body[128] had shadowed the body parameter — the user's draft — in the send-error path; -Werror=shadow refused the build, correctly, because the one thing that card must never do is confuse the error text with the text that failed to send. The touch worker sees the m: namespace and calls the fetch — which is also why that worker's stack is 12 KB, not 4: opening a conversation does a TLS handshake, a JSON parse, and a full card render on that stack, and mbedtls is the hungry part. (A prediction this page made earlier died honestly: this was expected to be "grammar v2" work. It shipped as grammar v1 — ordinary menu/list cards plus an id namespace turned out to be enough. The grammar grows when a card must look different, not when it must mean different.)

The badge costs nothing. The unread count rides the heartbeat the device already sends (wantUnread:"1", a string — the zod lesson), so the badge has no poll of its own. Home shows "Mail — n unread" with keep-last-on-absent semantics: a reply that omits the field keeps the last known number, and -1 ("never told") renders nothing rather than a lying zero. The e-ink discipline is the point: home re-renders only when the number changes while home is on glass — one refresh per change, zero per beat.

The feature's first form was an owner-side pusher (tiny_inbox.py, still useful as the notification path), and its design rules carried over intact:

  • Provenance is declared. Anything sent from the glass goes as the owner but marked "via sticky" — the agent/device sent it, not the owner's thumb. (This rule outlived its own plumbing: it began as an owner-side viaTiny flag when device tokens couldn't touch messages at all; the platform then grew the device-token rail and kept the marking.)
  • The read receipt is sacred. Fetching a thread marks it read platform-wide (that's the phone badge). A thread is only fetched when a human taps its row on the device; polling and the heartbeat badge use read-only forms.
  • Names survive the panel. Since 0.14.15 (on glass in 0.14.16) the renderer runs fold v2: a real UTF-8 codepoint decoder with a three-tier fold — a symbol table for the status glyphs agent prose uses daily (✓ ⚠ → ± ×), a systematic Latin-1 + Latin-Extended-A diacritic strip via packed range tables (é ñ ß Š ž readable), and emoji/CJK honestly folded to ? (refined in 0.16.8/R-4: emoji are tone, not content — stripped along with their plumbing (VS16, ZWJ, keycap) so "Hey! 👋" reads "Hey!" instead of the different sentence "Hey! ?"; CJK/unknown scripts keep ? because there position matters; status glyphs ✓ ⚠ ✅ ❌ sit inside emoji ranges but the symbol table folds them first, so [ok]/[!]/[x] still render). Turkish input rendered transliterated — "Çağatay" as "Cagatay" — until the extended-glyph bank landed; since 0.16.x it renders as written, and that claim is made below under this paragraph's own evidence rule. This line has been corrected twice, and the chain is worth keeping: the 0.14.15 commit said "Turkish set preserved" (it meant the transliteration mappings survived the v2 rewrite); this page amplified that into "renders as written"; a torture card then measured "Cagatay soyle" on glass; the first retraction blamed the font lookup; and a source-read finally settled it — the fold itself transliterates, deliberately, because the vendored font had ASCII glyphs only — at the time there were no ç pixels to draw. The claim lived in prose while the behavior lived in tables. True ç-pixels are a font-asset task, with the torture card as its regression fixture — the owner's name is the flagship case. The fix (first built as 0.14.19) implements exactly that: an extended font bank at 0x80–0x8B with 12 hand-drawn 5×7 glyphs (çğıöşü ÇĞİÖŞÜ — ı is i minus its dot bit; the cedilla is a 5-tall body plus a tail; breve and umlaut live on row 0), and a kCpFolds table that maps those twelve codepoints to the bank before the range tables run, so é still folds to e untouched. Compile-verified pre-push (sha 0f6ef35b). This paragraph has been wrong twice about this exact sentence — so it committed to saying "renders as written" only when the torture card passes on the physical panel, and not one iteration sooner. That pass exists: on 0.16.8-m14 (fw_commit 4dd7fcf7) the docs lane rendered the torture card over the relay and pulled the panel's own screenshot — "Çağatay çğıöşü ÇĞİÖŞÜ" renders with true cedillas, breves, dotless-ı and umlauts, while é ñ Š ž fold to their base letters and ✓ folds to [ok], exactly per design (receipt, 800×480 2-bit panel capture, 2026-08-26). The owner's name renders as written. It replaced a 22-entry byte-sequence allowlist, and malformed UTF-8 (truncated sequence, stray continuation byte) degrades to ? without desyncing the decoder. The review that shipped it caught its own Ext-A row-alignment bug (Ĵ/Ł/Š/Ž shifted two slots) before the glass ever saw it.
  • Human strings get defused — at both layers. The shell's action_for() substring-matches button strings to local actions — a correspondent named "Noble" or a message saying "sorun var" could silently press rescan ble / open the mic, while still reporting the tap. Pushers defuse human-authored labels, and since 0.14.6 the firmware only sniffs the label when a card gave no explicit id — a card that names its buttons has already said what they are. (Firmware's own bare-string buttons — Wi-Fi, Back, Home — keep working, which is exactly the case the sniff exists for.)

docs.title: The design language: physics first
docs.text:
Every failed UI idea on this project failed the same way — pretending the panel is an LCD. The working ideas all schedule around the panel. The latency budget, written on the wall:

event budget mechanism tap acknowledged < 50 ms buzzer — audio is the fast lane tap visually confirmed 300–500 ms partial refresh, region-sized page change 1–2 s full refresh (the metronome) relay verb round-trip 5–15 s poll cadence + agent turn ask with tools 10–60 s backend agent loop

The principle underneath: on e-ink, UI is a series of commitments, not a stream of frames. A phone UI animates toward a state; the Sticky declares states. That's why double-tap and drag were rejected in the touch audit — they're promises the panel can't keep. The shell only ships input verbs the panel can keep: tap, long-press, buttons, orientation — and time (cards that age gracefully).

Two more commitments already kept structurally:

  • Local-only zones — the keyboard's keystrokes are consumed by the shell and never posted upstream; only the outcome (joined the network, or didn't) leaves the device. A Wi-Fi password typed on the glass exists nowhere else.
  • A place, not a companion — the Sticky is the first embodiment of tiny that is bolted to a room instead of carried. It serves whoever stands in front of it, and its latency contract is glanceable, not interactive-first. The phone is the mobile terminal; the Sticky is the domestic one.

Where this is heading (direction, not shipped): a focus model where remote cards request the glass instead of seizing it, long-poll to replace the 5 s cadence, and IMU wake-on-lift gating the radio. The full thinking lives in THINKING.md.

docs.title: Streaming UI — the typer on e-ink
docs.text:
Provenance

This page is the root-level STREAMING_UI.md design document, included verbatim — it is the spec the feature was built against (grammar v3, shipped 0.15.x: the chat card, SSE ask, [streamed to glass] receipts). Written by the streaming lane; the docs site wraps it unedited so there is exactly one source of truth. Shipped-reality cross-references: chat card · ask verb.

docs.title: STREAMING_UI — the human-typer on e-ink
docs.text: Agent answers arrive on the glass the way tiny types on iOS: word by word, a caret blinking at the tail, the bubble settling with a final full refresh. Target: grammar v3, fw 0.15.x.

docs.title: Why this is possible (the physics budget)
docs.text:
operation cost source full mono refresh ~1–2 s sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() partial refresh ~300–500 ms sticky_display_refresh_partial() max stream commit rate ~2 Hz partial cost + panel busy-wait

Char-by-char is impossible; word/phrase-batched typewriter at ~2 Hz is comfortable and reads as intentional on e-ink — a telegram arriving, not a degraded phone. The fast path already exists: keyboard self-re-renders (same card_id) and scroll steps take refresh_partial() (tiny_display.cpp:1175). Streaming rides the SAME gate.

docs.title: Architecture (end to end)
docs.text:
backend (worker /device/ask)          firmware (esp32s3)
   ───────────────────────────           ─────────────────────────────
   POST {…, stream:"1"}       ──────►    tiny_node_do_ask_stream()
   ◄────── SSE: data:{"t":"…"}           esp_http_client_read() loop
           data:{"t":"…"}                  │ parse data: lines
           data:{"card":{…}}               ▼
           data:[DONE]                   tiny_display stream API
                                           stream_begin(title)   full refresh
                                           stream_append(delta)  buffer only
                                           stream_commit()       PARTIAL ≤2Hz
                                           stream_end(card?)     full refresh

Fallback chain: no stream:"1" support upstream → plain JSON reply → the existing blocking path renders once. The stream is an enhancement, never a requirement — a device on old backend behaves exactly like 0.14.x.

docs.title: Layer 1 — display: the stream card (firmware/main/tiny_display.cpp)
docs.text:
New extern-C API (tiny/tiny_display.h):

// Begin a streaming text card: draws chrome (title bar, glance cluster,
// empty body, caret) with ONE FULL refresh and enters stream mode.
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_begin(const char *title, const char *card_id);
// Append UTF-8 text to the stream buffer. Cheap; no drawing. Returns
// ESP_ERR_NO_MEM past the 8000-byte reply cap (excess dropped, marked).
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_append(const char *text);
// Re-render body + caret via the PARTIAL path. Callers rate-limit; this
// also self-limits to >=400ms between commits (drop-coalesce, never queue).
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_commit(void);
// Leave stream mode: final render WITHOUT caret, FULL refresh (clears the
// partial-ghosting), publish tap regions. `final_card_json` optional — when
// the answer carried a ```card``` block it replaces the text card entirely.
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_end(const char *final_card_json);
bool tiny_display_stream_active(void);

docs.title: Rules (each one is a lesson this repo already paid for)
docs.text:
1. Same card_id per commit → partial refresh. Extend the kb_rerender || s_scroll_partial gate with s_stream_partial.
  2. Full refresh at end is mandatory — 20+ consecutive partials ghost on the SSD1677; the closing wipe is the "bubble settles" moment.
  3. No tap regions until stream_end. Mid-stream layout is unsettled; publishing early violates the publish-after-refresh honesty rule.
  4. Caret = 3px fill_rect DarkGray at the text tail (keyboard caret idiom), drawn only while streaming.
  5. Auto-scroll to tail each commit when content overflows the body box (tiny_display_scroll(1<<20) idiom from render_thread) — the human reads the newest words, like every chat app.
  6. UTF-8 boundary discipline: a delta may split a multibyte char. Buffer holds raw bytes; an incomplete trailing sequence is held back from fold (clip_utf8 idiom) and completed by the next append.
  7. Stream mode owns the display: render_card during an active stream ends the stream first (a relay envelope outranks a typer animation).
  8. Rotation mid-stream: commit path inherits the rot_changed full-wipe guard automatically (same render funnel).

docs.title: State (file-static, next to the scroll state)
docs.text:
static bool   s_stream_on = false;
static bool   s_stream_partial = false;      // commit -> partial gate
static char  *s_stream_buf = NULL;           // PSRAM, REPLY_MAX cap
static size_t s_stream_len = 0, s_stream_cap = 0;
static char   s_stream_title[64];
static char   s_stream_cid[24];
static int64_t s_stream_last_commit_us = 0;  // 400ms floor

Renders go through the normal tiny_display_render_card() funnel with a synthesized {"type":"text",...} spec + a s_stream_caret flag the text renderer reads — ONE render path, no forked drawing code.

docs.title: Layer 2 — wire: SSE ask (firmware/main/tiny_node.cpp)
docs.text:
tiny_node_do_ask_stream(text, voice_secs, out, out_cap):

  • Body gains "stream":"1" (string — the zod idiom).
  • Open with esp_http_client_open() + fetch_headers + chunked esp_http_client_read() (exact pattern of tiny_ota.cpp's download loop).
  • Content-Type: text/event-stream → parse data: lines:
  • {"t":"<delta>"} → stream_append + flush policy
  • {"card":{...}} → save as final card
  • {"error":"..."} → honest error card (existing askfail idiom)
  • [DONE] → stream_end(card)
  • Flush policy: commit when (pending bytes > 0) AND (≥400 ms since last commit) — checked after each read; word batching falls out naturally from the 2 Hz floor.
  • Content-Type is NOT event-stream → body is the old JSON shape → fall through to the existing render-once path. One firmware, both backends.
  • Voice asks stream too (recording happens before the request as today).
  • 15 s stall watchdog per read (a hung stream must not hold the panel); on stall: stream_end(NULL) + append " [stream stalled]" — a cut answer must say it is cut.

Callers: dispatch("ask …"), dispatch("voice …") and the AI button worker switch to the streaming engine; reply/summary semantics unchanged.

docs.title: Layer 3 — backend: SSE on /device/ask
docs.text:
Files: ~/tinyai-id/chatgpt-plugin-tinyai/src/ask.ts + app/api/devices/ask/route.ts

  • stream:"1" in the body → reply text/event-stream: 
    data: {"t":"Hello "}
data: {"t":"from the "}
data: {"t":"fridge."}
data: {"card":{"type":"kv",...}}   ← only when a ```card``` block emerged
data: [DONE]
  • The worker already streams internally from the model (job-run pipeline); today it buffers to one JSON. The SSE arm forwards deltas AND still runs extractCard() over the accumulated text at the end (card blocks are lifted out; card-fence text is withheld from the delta stream — the device must not type raw JSON at the human, so deltas pause when a ``` fence opens and the fenced content ships only as the final card event).
  • Next.js proxy: runtime='nodejs' already; pipe the worker stream through (ReadableStream passthrough), don't await json().
  • Non-stream callers see byte-identical behavior. Old firmware never sends the flag. No breaking change anywhere.

docs.title: Layer 4 — chat chrome (the iOS look, translated to 4-gray)
docs.text:
From ios/DESIGN.md + Theme.swift, honest e-ink equivalents:

iOS Sticky .tinyCard() 14pt radius + accent hairline rounded-rect border (new draw_round_rect, Bresenham corners) + DarkGray hairline user bubble: accent 22%, 18pt radius LightGray fill, right-aligned assistant bubble: secondary bg White fill + Black outline, left-aligned StatusDot filled/hollow already shape-based — copy as-is status bar existing glance cluster (time/battery/wifi)

New card type chat (spec v1.1): 

{"type":"chat","card_id":"ask","messages":[
  {"role":"user","body":"what's the weather"},
  {"role":"assistant","body":"Sunny, 24C."}
]}
The streaming ask renders as a chat card: user bubble immediately (echo of the question — the receipt), assistant bubble streams into place. Scroll + buttons + fold all inherited (body renderer registered in render_body()).

Layer 4 ships after 1–3; the typer works on the plain text card first.

docs.title: Version & consumer gates
docs.text:
• TINY_GRAMMAR_VERSION → 3 (new chat type + streaming ask are v3 claims).
  • Heartbeat capabilities unchanged (ask verb is the same verb).
  • Dashboard: no change needed (relay replies unchanged); the mirror simply shows a caret mid-answer when screenshotted — which is true.

docs.title: Delivery plan
docs.text:
• M-S0 this document
  • M-S1 display stream API (stream_begin/append/commit/end) + caret
  • M-S2 firmware SSE ask engine + fallback + dispatch wiring
  • M-S3 backend SSE arm (worker ask.ts + app proxy) — 22/22 tests
  • M-S4 on-glass proof (2026-08-25 22:2xZ, fw 0.15.1-m13): relay envelope ask …duck on a fridge → stream begin 33.9s, 7 partial commits at ~0.98s cadence (33.9→41.9s serial log), stream end -> ESP_OK, reply "…[streamed to glass]". Glass evidence: https://plugin.tiny.technology/media/c4f03565-0d4b-4c17-a070-3d901179f60e.png
  • M-S5 chat card + bubbles (0.15.3-m13, proven on glass): type=chat renders iOS bubbles on 4-gray — user = LightGray fill right-aligned, assistant = outlined white left, radius 12, measure-then-paint via the one draw_wrapped. Streamed text asks render as chat (question = user bubble receipt, answer types into the assistant bubble); 10 chat commits at ~1.1s cadence in the proof run. Bonus fix: do_ask gained a cross-caller single-flight mutex (the M-S5 proof caught a ghost AI-button ask interleaving with a relay ask — two writers, one panel). Glass: https://plugin.tiny.technology/media/dfc23817-8184-4dc4-b8b5-5b3b39aa7ee6.png
  • M-S6 grammar v3 (shipped with M-S2) + docs: cards.md chat type, commands.md streaming ask

docs.title: Honesty rules for this feature
docs.text:
• A stalled stream says "[stream stalled]" on the glass — never a silent tail.
  • The caret exists ONLY while bytes may still arrive; a caret on a dead stream is a lie about liveness.
  • Buttons appear only when the answer is complete — a Reply button on a half-arrived answer invites replying to words that may change.
  • The final full refresh is the contract that what you read is what stays.

docs.title: Troubleshooting — the field guide
docs.text: Every entry here is a defect actually observed on this hardware during bring-up, with its root cause and the fix now shipped in the firmware. Symptoms first, because that is what you have.

docs.title: A card I sent never appears — and the reply was silence
docs.text:
Relay envelopes are delivered once. If the firmware consumed the envelope while a bug prevented handling it, that envelope is gone — re-invoke after any fix, don't wait for a retry that will never come.

Historical root cause (fixed in 0.3.1-m3): the relay delivers payload as a serialized JSON string, not a nested object. Firmware that reads it as an object skips every envelope silently. Current firmware parses the string form, tolerates the object form, and replies unparseable envelope instead of nothing.

docs.title: A kv card renders as a title, a footer, and a void
docs.text: The renderer reads the key rows — not kv. Since 0.9.6-m9 a kv card without rows says so on the panel instead of drawing a convincing empty card, and rows that don't fit are counted and admitted (+N did not fit) rather than vanishing.

docs.title: Dashes and other punctuation render as ???
docs.text: The font is ASCII-only (known limitation, logged — not a bug to report). Keep card text ASCII; — becomes ??? on the glass.

docs.title: I don't trust what the panel shows
docs.text: Neither do we — that's why the screenshot verb exists. It uploads the actual framebuffer as a hosted PNG: render ground truth, not a belief about the last card sent. render_ui replies echo card_id=<id> — the id the panel actually committed.

docs.title: Phantom taps right after boot
docs.text: GT911 ghost touches. Fixed in 0.4.0-m4: a real finger spans several 30 ms polls, ghosts don't (2-poll debounce), plus a boot grace window (5000 ms originally, tuned to 1200 ms once points with size > 0 were trusted on first poll).

docs.title: A tap lands on the wrong button (or label=? in the event feed)
docs.text: The stale-region race, closed in 0.9.x: hit-regions used to be published at draw time, up to ~2 s before the e-ink actually displayed them. Regions now build into a staging table and publish atomically with the card commit — a tap is always hit-tested against the card that is really on the glass.

docs.title: The device goes silent after a horizontal swipe (fixed in 0.16.5 — kill sequence replayed on glass, device survived)
docs.text:
The batch-#4 P0, and the diagnosis published here first ("crashes, reboots clean") was wrong on the failure mode: the device never rebooted — it wedged. Root cause: tiny_shell_cycle computed its modulus over all 6 page-enum entries when the ring contract was 4 — silently wrong ever since WIFI/BLE were appended to the enum (M10.2). A mid-content swipe on the pushed wifi card ring-nexted into the BLE page: NimBLE first-time bring-up + a 4 s scan + two blocking e-ink renders, unrequested, on the act task, with Wi-Fi live on the same radio — and every later relay envelope sat pending forever behind it. (The swipe's own receipt still came back, because the reply writes before the render path runs — a receipt is not proof the consequence survived.)

Fixed three ways in 0.16.5: the ring mods over its 4 roots only (a static_assert pins the enum; drill pages refuse cycling with a double blip), the pushed-card cell is an announced dead-end (double blip, NOT_ALLOWED) instead of undefined behavior — refined in 0.16.7: mid-content right now pops to the parent over a radio-free path (the crash family stays unreachable), only left remains the dead-end, and a wedge watchdog on the node task — which survived the original wedge — reboots after 45 s of one stuck gesture route (10× the worst honest route) into the rollback-armed boot path, posting a device_note first. A gesture bug now costs one reboot, never the relay. Identity and Wi-Fi survive either way — NVS is untouched.

Verified, not just built: the exact batch-#4 killing sequence was replayed on 0.16.5 (page wifi → mid-content ← swipe → status): the card stayed wifi, the relay kept answering, uptime ran unbroken through the probes. One release-discipline footnote from the same session: that first 0.16.5 artifact reported fw_commit e1fac273-dirty — the taint was another lane's uncommitted dashboard files sweeping into git describe at build time (firmware source was clean), filed as a P1: rebuild from a clean snapshot and republish, because a channel pointer must equal a source commit.

docs.title: ask failed (422): nothing transcribed
docs.text: Not a bug — the recording contained no usable speech (a press with silence, or speech too short for the transcriber). The firmware logs the backend body, replies with it, and paints an honest "didn't catch that — hold the AI button and talk to me" card (card_id=askfail). Hold the AI button and speak a full sentence.

docs.title: ask failed: couldn't reach tiny (was: Backend said: -1)
docs.text: The question never left the device — TLS/socket setup or the HTTP write failed locally (network hiccup, or heap pressure at handshake time). Since 0.16.1 the firmware retries once after 400 ms (safe precisely because nothing was delivered — a resend can't produce a second answer to one question) and, if that fails too, says so honestly. On firmware before 0.16.1 the same failure surfaced as "ask failed / Backend said: -1" with an empty body — a wording bug that blamed the backend for a sentence it never said (-1 was the local HTTP client's sentinel, not a backend status). If you see that phrasing, the fix is ota, and the fault to chase is the device's network or free heap, not tiny.

docs.title: The mic is deaf after the device slept
docs.text: The ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for USB-Serial-JTAG on deep-sleep wake, muting the PDM mic. Fixed in 0.9.5: the mux is reclaimed before every capture (idempotent). Prove liveness without a human: miccheck 2 replies real RMS/peak numbers — a dead mux reads flat zeros.

docs.title: Heartbeat gets a 401
docs.text: One 401 never wipes identity (that brick risk is dead since 0.9.1-m9). The device needs 3+ consecutive 401s spanning 5 minutes to enter auth-halted mode — a slow 5-minute heartbeat cadence, auth_halted exposed in status, and a "back online" card when the token works again. NVS is never erased in the node loop.

docs.title: The device is asleep and won't answer the relay
docs.text: A sleeping device's radio is off. There is no wake verb and cannot be one — only the AI button (EXT1) or the sleep timer wakes it. sleep <sec> replies before sleeping for exactly this reason.

docs.title: The portal never appears
docs.text: The provisioning portal (softAP tiny-XXXX, key tinysetup, 192.168.4.1) is boot-gated on zero stored networks — a provisioned device deliberately never enters it. It reopens automatically after the 401 auth-halted path concludes the token is revoked.

docs.title: Opening the serial port reboots the chip
docs.text: The CH343 asserts DTR/RTS on open, and toggles the lines again on close — any serial open/close resets the chip, even opened with both low. The port is for flashing and recovery only; the relay is the production path. (Development iterates over OTA — 9 updates shipped in one day without a cable.)

docs.title: ota replies "already up to date"
docs.text:
The channel pointer matches the running version — push a new manifest first. A staged update sha256-verifies, replies then reboots into a rollback-armed trial: if the trial image can't reach a heartbeat 200, the previous slot boots instead.

Something not covered here? The raw bring-up ledger with every defect and its evidence lives in docs/JOURNAL.md (repo access required).

docs.title: Firmware implementation-depth audit — 2026-08-25 ~21:50Z (main-session tiny)
docs.text: Bar: "iPhone-like experience" per cagatay. Four parallel deep-read auditors. - TOUCH_AUDIT.md (done): P0 stale-region race root-caused; P0 no tap feedback wired. - DISPLAY_AUDIT.md (done): P0 no display mutex; P0 refresh policy documented-but-absent; P0 font metrics wrong; card spec ~half implemented; NO UTF-8. - NETWORK_AUDIT.md + SYSTEM_AUDIT.md: auditors running (batch_mt979diwa7503042), reports land here. STRUCTURAL GAP: tiny_provision/tiny_boot/tiny_stream/tiny_commands are headers with NO .cpp — softAP portal does not exist; device cannot be re-provisioned without serial.

docs.title: Display + Rendering Stack Audit — 2026-08-25 (auditor 2, full read)
docs.text: Files read in full: tiny_display.cpp (278L), canvas.cpp/h, font.cpp/h, sticky_display.cpp/h, tiny/tiny_display.h, plus render paths in tiny_main.cpp, tiny_node.cpp, tiny_touch.cpp, tiny_screenshot.cpp, and the card spec in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:54-80.

docs.title: P0 — correctness / safety
docs.text:
P0-1: No display mutex — three tasks call tiny_display_render_card() concurrently. Evidence: tiny_main.cpp:129 (serial card console, app_main task), tiny_node.cpp:168/178/198 (node task), and the touch task reads s_regions (tiny_display.cpp:113-117) while renders rewrite them. Zero locking anywhere (grep mutex|semaphore → nothing). Consequences: (a) interleaved Canvas draws + SSD1677 SPI transactions (commit blocks on BUSY up to 10s, sticky_display.cpp:126) — torn frames; (b) torn button-region reads; (c) snapshot_gray8 can capture a half-drawn canvas. Fix: one render task owning the display (ARCHITECTURE.md task table line 103 already promises this — "render | core 1 | owns display"), fed by a queue; or minimally a SemaphoreHandle_t around canvas+refresh+regions.

P0-2: The documented refresh policy does not exist. tiny/tiny_display.h:3-5 and ARCHITECTURE.md:80 promise "min 1.5s between refreshes; coalesce bursts". Implementation: every render calls sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() unconditionally (tiny_display.cpp:210); tiny_display.cpp:14-15 admits it in a comment. A burst of relay envelopes = flicker storm + panel stress. Fix: render task records last_refresh_tick; early card replaces the pending card (coalesce = keep newest), delay to the 1.5s boundary.

P0-3: Font metrics contradiction — layout math assumes a font that doesn't exist. tiny_display.cpp:36-39 declares kGlyphW=8, kGlyphH=16. The actual font is 5x7 with advance (5+1)*scale and height 7*scale (font.h:9-11, canvas.cpp:115). Effects: text_width() overestimates 33% → button labels left of center (tiny_display.cpp:104-106); chars_per_line underestimates 25% → ~19% of usable width wasted; line pitch 38px for a 14px glyph = 24px dead leading; title bar reserves 58px for a 21px title. Sparse and small simultaneously. Fix: derive all metrics from kFontWidth/kFontHeight/kFontSpacing — or replace the font (P1-1) and keep the 8x16 cell for real.

P0-4: Card spec v1 is ~half implemented — chart, image, composite, button objects, card_id, gray4 all missing. Implemented (tiny_display.cpp:196-206): only text/list/kv + unknown-type fallback. Specifically: - buttons as objects: draw_buttons line 96 does cJSON_IsString(b) ? b->valuestring : "?" — the spec's own example {"id":"done","label":"Done ✓"} renders as a button labeled ?. And ui_tap events post label= only (tiny_touch.cpp:78-84), never {card_id, button_id} (ARCHITECTURE.md:73) — the backend can't correlate taps to cards. This is plausibly the live label=? bug. - chart: not implemented — unknown-type branch (line 201). A bar chart is ~40 lines with fill_rect. - image: tiny_display_blit_1bit exists (line 236) but nothing calls it; no HTTP fetch path; partial flag ignored (line 238). - composite: absent. - gray4 hint: never read; every draw uses GrayLevel::Black only; mono conversion maps DarkGray→black, LightGray→white (sticky_display.cpp:63) — the 4-gray panel runs as a 1-bit panel 100% of the time. sticky_display_refresh() (gray4) has zero callers. Priority order: button-objects + card_id/button_id in ui_tap (protocol correctness, small) → chart → image fetch → composite.

docs.title: P1 — visible quality
docs.text:
P1-1: 5x7 font at 235ppi is nowhere near "iPhone-like". font.cpp is the classic 5x7 ASCII set, integer-scaled into square blocks (canvas.cpp:104-112, no smoothing; 4 gray levels unused for anti-aliasing). Fix: embed a proportional anti-aliased bitmap font (TTF converted at 2 sizes, 2bpp glyphs — 2bpp maps 1:1 onto the 4-gray canvas = free anti-aliasing). Single highest-leverage polish item.

P1-2: No UTF-8 — Turkish text renders as garbage ?s. font_get_glyph(char) (font.cpp:117-124) treats every byte ≥0x7F as ?. "Çağatay" renders ??a?atay (two ? per multibyte char). "Done ✓" → Done ???. Fix: UTF-8 decode in draw_text + Latin-ext block for çğıöşüÇĞİÖŞÜ (12 glyphs) + symbols (✓ ✗ ° … → •). Cheap, high emotional value for this user.

P1-3: Embedded in body text renders as ? glyphs. draw_wrapped (tiny_display.cpp:45-72) chunks by char count; inside a chunk → font_get_glyph(' ') → ?. Line 69 only catches newline at a wrap boundary. Fix: hard-break on (and ) before wrap math.

P1-4: Truncation is silent — overflow text just vanishes. draw_wrapped stops at max_y (line 52), list/kv rows break past max_y (lines 130, 146). No ellipsis, no "+3 more", no pagination. Fix: clipped content draws a …more marker; long-term page with UP/DOWN hardware buttons (GPIO5/6 already initialized, tiny_main.cpp:78).

P1-5: Touch regions published before the frame is on glass — see TOUCH_AUDIT P0-1; the fix must pair regions+card_id with the committed frame under the render lock.

P1-6: Partial refresh implemented in the driver, never used; no ghosting counter. sticky_display_refresh_partial() (sticky_display.cpp:186-212, correct comparison-frame trick documented) has no callers. When status bar/stream land: add s_partial_count, force full refresh every ~8-12 partials and on card-type changes.

docs.title: P2 — robustness / nits
docs.text:
• P2-1 draw_wrapped back-off loop bounded only by take=strlen clamp — comment/bound to prevent regression (tiny_display.cpp:55-59).
  • P2-2 line[128] silently truncates if chars_per_line > 127 — derive buffer from constant.
  • P2-3 snapshot_gray8 reads the live canvas, not "the LAST RENDERED framebuffer" as the header claims (tiny/tiny_display.h:20-21). Rotation IS consistent across canvas/touch/screenshot ✓. Snapshot under the render lock after a successful commit makes the claim true.
  • P2-4 tiny_display_blit_1bit = 384,000 per-pixel calls with bounds checks — row-wise byte expansion ~20× faster; matters for stream.
  • P2-5 splash() magic coordinates only center because of the wrong 8px metric; will shift when P0-3 lands.
  • P2-6 Footer reserves 26px for a 7px line — same metric bug family.
  • P2-7 kv value column fixed at 360 (tiny_display.cpp:141) — long keys overlap values; size from longest key.
  • P2-8 Unknown-type fallback paints honestly ✓ but should also carry "unsupported type" upstream in the reply.

docs.title: Status bar (clock / battery / Wi-Fi) — what it needs
docs.text:
1. Reserved strip (e.g. top 28px) the card renderer must not paint — add content_top offset (today render_card clears the whole canvas, tiny_display.cpp:172).
  2. Partial refresh — driver ready (sticky_display.h:20-23); strip must be pure B/W.
  3. Ghosting budget — full refresh every N strip updates.
  4. Data sources — sticky_battery_read() exists; tiny_wifi_is_up(); clock via SNTP or the on-board PCF8563 RTC (I2C1).
  5. The render-task/queue from P0-1 — housekeeping posts "strip dirty" events, never touches SPI.

docs.title: Polish roadmap (ranked)
docs.text:
1. Render task + queue + 1.5s coalescing lock (P0-1, P0-2) — prerequisite for everything.
  2. Region/frame atomicity + button {id,label} + ui_tap {card_id,button_id} (P1-5, P0-4a) — kills today's field bug.
  3. Font metrics truth pass (P0-3).
  4. Real font: proportional, 2bpp anti-aliased, UTF-8 + Turkish glyphs (P1-1, P1-2) — the visible leap.
  5. \n handling + …more truncation marker (P1-3, P1-4).
  6. chart card (small, high demo value).
  7. Status bar on partial refresh + ghosting counter.
  8. image card (HTTP fetch → fast blit) then stream (P2-4).
  9. gray4:true path — actually use the 4-gray panel.
  10. composite card — closes card-spec v1.
  11. Nits: kv column sizing, splash re-centering, snapshot-after-commit semantics.

docs.title: NETWORK + NODE + OTA Stack Audit — firmware/main
docs.text: Auditor: tiny (sub-agent #1/2), 2026-08-25. Scope: tiny_node.cpp (363L), tiny_wifi.cpp (79L), tiny_ota.cpp (188L), tiny_upload.cpp (95L), tiny_config.cpp (193L), all headers in tiny/, plus tiny_main.cpp for the boot wiring. fw version at audit: 0.8.1-m8.

docs.title: P0-1 · 401 → forget_identity() + reboot with NO provisioning portal = permanent brick
docs.text:
• tiny_node.cpp:264-268 (relay poll) and tiny_node.cpp:308-312 (heartbeat): a single HTTP 401 wipes device_id/token from NVS and calls esp_restart().
  • tiny/tiny_provision.h declares tiny_provision_start() — there is no implementation anywhere in the tree (grep confirms zero references outside the header). After the wipe, the fresh boot lands in tiny_main.cpp:90-94 — "waiting for device_id+token (config incomplete)" — a state recoverable only over a serial cable ({"config":{...}} line console, tiny_main.cpp:96+).
  • Threat model: 401 does not only mean "owner revoked me". A backend auth deploy bug, token-store hiccup, or misrouted request that answers 401 once destroys a good identity irreversibly. The comment at tiny_node.cpp:3-4 even admits the portal is a future milestone ("-> portal once M3b lands") while the wipe is live today.
  • Compounding bug: tiny_config_forget_identity() → rewrite_without() (tiny_config.cpp:167-190) returns an error if tiny_config_load fails (e.g. corrupt blob), the caller ignores the return and reboots anyway → potential 401→reboot→401 hammer loop against the backend.
  • Fix (minimum shippable): require N (≥3) consecutive 401s across ≥60s before wiping; never wipe while tiny_provision_start is unimplemented — degrade to a "re-auth needed" card + slow retry instead; check forget_identity()'s return before restarting.

docs.title: P0-2 · Wi-Fi drop is unrecoverable at runtime; all-networks-fail at boot parks the device forever
docs.text:
• tiny_wifi.cpp:24-30: on WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED the handler retries esp_wifi_connect() exactly 2 times (s_retries < 2), then sets the FAILED bit and stops. After boot, nothing ever waits on that bit and nothing ever calls tiny_wifi_connect() again — s_up stays false forever.
  • tiny_node.cpp:304: the node task's only reaction to wifi-down is vTaskDelay(2000); continue; — an infinite polite wait for a flag no one will ever set. Router reboots → device is offline until battery death or a power cycle, silently, with a stale card on the e-ink.
  • Boot path: tiny_main.cpp:84; if every SSID fails, tiny_wifi_connect returns ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_CONNECT (tiny_wifi.cpp:75-76) and app_main just logs it — no retry loop, no backoff-and-rejoin, no portal (see P0-1). One bad radio moment at power-on = offline appliance.
  • Detail: s_retries is written from the wifi event task and reset from the caller task with no synchronization (tiny_wifi.cpp:19,66) — benign today, racy once reconnect logic lands.
  • Fix: a supervisor path — when !tiny_wifi_is_up() for >30s, re-run the roaming list with exponential backoff (30s→5min cap); at boot, retry the join loop instead of giving up once.

docs.title: P0-3 · Relay envelopes silently LOST when the poll response overflows 4 KB (matches the observed "no reply after 45s" bug)
docs.text:
• tiny_node.cpp:300: response buffer is static char resp[4096], while poll_relay asks for up to 5 messages (tiny_node.cpp:262, max:5). One render_ui envelope with a real card spec can approach the size alone.
  • http_evt (tiny_node.cpp:48-58) drops whole chunks once len + data_len >= cap → truncated JSON → cJSON_Parse returns NULL → poll_relay returns silently (tiny_node.cpp:270-271).
  • The backend hands envelopes out on the PUT — a dropped parse means those envelopes are consumed server-side and never dispatched, never replied to. The sender waits out its full 45s timeout. This is the exact symptom cagatay and the supervisor both hit today (411a887c…). It also violates the firmware's own stated rule (tiny_node.cpp:292: "never silence").
  • Fix: raise the buffer (PSRAM, 16–32 KB) and make truncation loud: track a truncated flag in sink_t; on truncation, retry with max:1, and reply "envelope too large" rather than dropping. Consider max:1 permanently — the loop runs every 5s anyway.

docs.title: P0-4 · Declared-but-never-defined inventory (headers with zero implementation)
docs.text:
Confirmed by grep across all .c/.cpp: the only mentions are in comments.

Header Declared, never defined Product impact tiny/tiny_provision.h tiny_provision_start() No softAP portal. Device cannot be (re)provisioned without a serial cable — combined with P0-1 this is the not-shippable pair. iOS onboarding path does not exist. tiny/tiny_boot.h tiny_boot_early(), tiny_boot_wake_cause(), tiny_boot_is_trial(), tiny_boot_commit(), tiny_boot_deep_sleep() No deep sleep / power management at all. Latent mic-killer: tiny_audio.cpp:4 says the post-deep-sleep USB-JTAG pin-reclaim fix (GPIO19/20 release + mic-rail cycle, docs/RESEARCH.md §6) "is handled in tiny_boot_early()" — a function that does not exist. The day deep sleep lands, voice ask dies after every wake unless this is remembered. OTA judging meanwhile lives in tiny_node.cpp:317-325 (works, but contradicts the header's "ONLY tiny_boot judges" contract). tiny/tiny_stream.h tiny_stream_image(), tiny_stream_play(), tiny_stream_stop() No image/frame-stream rendering — the WiFi-native media plan (#778) has no device half. tiny/tiny_commands.h tiny_commands_dispatch() Command table split-brain: dispatch is hand-rolled inside tiny_node.cpp:193-257 with only render_ui/status/ask/voice/screenshot/ota. The header promises say, sensors, image, stream, sleep, wake, reprovision, help. The heartbeat advertises "say" as a capability (tiny_node.cpp:110) that the dispatcher cannot execute — an agent will call it and get "unknown command".

docs.title: P1 — fix before calling it stable
docs.text:
1. hb_fail is dead code. tiny_node.cpp:302,313 — counted, never read. No escalation exists for a failing backend: no backoff, no wifi re-join, no reboot-after-N-hours. Wire it to the P0-2 supervisor (e.g. `hb_fail

    = 10→ re-run wifi join;>= 40` → reboot).

  2. No retry/backoff on any HTTP call. Every call in tiny_node.cpp/tiny_upload.cpp/tiny_ota.cpp is single-shot. Timeouts ARE consistently set (15s default tiny_node.cpp:42, 30s upload/OTA tiny_upload.cpp:74/tiny_ota.cpp:127, 80s ask tiny_node.cpp:158) — good — but one lost packet fails a heartbeat/reply/event outright. Replies (tiny_node.cpp:130) deserve 1–2 retries: a lost reply = the sender's 45s timeout even though the work was done.
  3. OTA version check trusts a hand-maintained string. tiny_ota.cpp:111 does strcmp(ver, TINY_FW_VERSION) where TINY_FW_VERSION lives in tiny/tiny_version.h ("0.8.1-m8") and must be bumped by hand each build. Forgotten bump → device reports "already up to date" forever and the channel is wedged (ESP_ERR_INVALID_VERSION, tiny_node.cpp:245-246). Fix: compare the manifest sha256 against the running partition's image hash (esp_partition_get_sha256 / esp_app_desc), or generate the version from git at build time (git describe → configure_file). Version-string-in-git is the same trap the Nicla hit.
  4. Node loop is fully serialized — one slow call starves everything. dispatch() runs inline in node_task; an ask blocks up to 80s (tiny_node.cpp:158), during which heartbeat (due every 30s) and relay poll stop → platform may mark the device offline mid-question, and other queued envelopes wait. Event drain (tiny_node.cpp:331-337) POSTs inline too: 8 queued taps × 15s timeout against a sick backend = 2min stall. Consider a worker task for ask, or at least accept the tradeoff in docs.
  5. Event queue drops silently on overflow / wifi-down. tiny_node.cpp:39 EVENT_QUEUE_LEN 8; tiny_node.cpp:362 xQueueSend(..., 0) → overflow returns ESP_ERR_NO_MEM and the tap vanishes (tap #9 while offline is gone forever). Queue is only drained when wifi is up. Acceptable for ui_tap, but log a drop counter and surface it in status.

docs.title: P2 — hygiene / hardening
docs.text:
1. ask_resp[8192] truncation (tiny_node.cpp:156): a long answer + card overflows → parse fail → user sees "(no text)" though HTTP was 200. Same silent-truncation pattern as P0-3; same fix (flag + honest message).
  2. resp[0] guard: poll_relay checks !resp[0] (tiny_node.cpp:269) — fine, but a non-JSON 200 body is also silently ignored; log it.
  3. URL buffers char url[160] (tiny_node.cpp:63, tiny_upload.cpp:65, tiny_ota.cpp:60): fine for https://tiny.technology, but a long custom api value silently truncates the URL → requests to a half-path. Guard snprintf return.
  4. OTA has no resume — a failed 3MB download restarts from byte 0 (tiny_ota.cpp:152-159). Acceptable on wifi; note it.
  5. OTA read_pointer reads status after failed perform (tiny_ota.cpp:77-83) — harmless but returns err vs ESP_FAIL inconsistently with http_json_t (-1 convention).
  6. Rollback window: a trial image that runs but never heartbeats 200 stays PENDING_VERIFY indefinitely — rollback only happens at the next reset. Pair with a "no heartbeat 200 within 10min while trial → reboot" rule in the (unimplemented) tiny_boot judge.
  7. Wifi creds + device token in plaintext NVS (tiny_config.cpp), no NVS encryption mentioned in sdkconfig review scope. Physical-access threat only; note for later.
  8. esp_wifi_stop() between roaming attempts (tiny_wifi.cpp:64) while the event handler may still fire esp_wifi_connect() — benign race, tidy when P0-2 lands.

docs.title: What's GOOD (keep)
docs.text:
• Every HTTP call has an explicit timeout; none can hang forever (the Nicla's 4.5-min silent hang lesson is applied).
  • OTA: host allowlist (tiny_ota.cpp:28-31), streamed download with size check against the slot, sha256 verified before esp_ota_set_boot_partition, rollback armed, validity marked only on first heartbeat 200 (tiny_node.cpp:317-325) — a genuinely correct A/B design.
  • Reply-before-reboot on ota verb (tiny_node.cpp:242-244).
  • Event queue decouples touch ISR path from HTTP (producer never blocks).
  • Upload builds its body in PSRAM and never logs the token.
  • Unknown envelope commands answer help text instead of silence (tiny_node.cpp:252-256).

docs.title: SYSTEM + BOOT + POWER + AUDIO Audit — firmware/main
docs.text: Auditor: tiny (sub-agent #2), 2026-08-25. Scope: tiny_main.cpp board.cpp sticky_power.cpp sticky_battery.cpp sticky_buzzer.cpp tiny_audio.cpp tiny_button.cpp pin_config.h (+ tiny_node.cpp/tiny_wifi.cpp read where the power story required it).

docs.title: P0-1 · tiny_boot.cpp does not exist; the USB-JTAG GPIO19/20 mic-mux fix is NOWHERE in the tree
docs.text:
• tiny/tiny_boot.h:14 declares tiny_boot_early(void); tiny_audio.cpp:4 and tiny/tiny_audio.h:4 claim "the Voice Companion deep-sleep lesson … is handled in tiny_boot_early()". There is no tiny_boot.cpp — not in main/CMakeLists.txt SRCS, not anywhere. grep -rn usb_pad_enable|USB_SERIAL_JTAG|gpio_reset_pin matches only comments/headers.
  • The known hardware bug (community-verified on this exact board): after deep-sleep wake, the S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for native USB-Serial-JTAG → PDM mic is deaf on every post-sleep voice attempt. Required fix at earliest boot: USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable = 0 + gpio_reset_pin(GPIO19/20) (+ the GPIO38 rail clean-cycle, which tiny_audio_record_wav does do, tiny_audio.cpp:63).
  • Latent today only because deep sleep is also never entered (P0-2). The moment P0-2 lands, voice breaks after the first wake. Also: tiny_boot.h promises the OTA trial/commit judge (tiny_boot_is_trial/tiny_boot_commit) — that logic was instead inlined into tiny_node.cpp:317-325, so the header is a lie; either implement the module or fix the docs/headers.

docs.title: P0-2 · Deep sleep is unreachable — zero callers, no idle timeout, no power-off gesture
docs.text:
• sticky_power_enter_deep_sleep() (sticky_power.cpp:47) is well-written (holds latch, kills EPD/touch/mic/SD/buzzer rails, EXT1 ANY_LOW wake on GPIO4) but has no call site anywhere. tiny_boot_deep_sleep() (tiny_boot.h:24) is unimplemented.
  • No inactivity timer (stock fw sleeps at 2 min idle), no long-press power-off (tiny_button.cpp:50 sets long_press_time = 2000 but registers only BUTTON_SINGLE_CLICK, tiny_button.cpp:57), and the M2 demo card literally shows a "Sleep" button (tiny_main.cpp:50) with no handler behind it.
  • Consequence: Wi-Fi + CPU run 24/7 → the 750 mAh pack dies in roughly half a day (see battery section), then hard-cuts with no warning.

docs.title: P0-3 · No low-battery protection at all
docs.text:
• sticky_battery_read() is called in exactly one place: the status verb's string (tiny_node.cpp:203-204). Nothing polls SoC periodically; nothing triggers a "battery low" card, an event to the backend, or a protective sticky_power_enter_deep_sleep() at ~5 %.
  • With P0-2 (always-on Wi-Fi) this guarantees repeated deep discharge of the 750 mAh cell — a battery-longevity and data-loss (mid-OTA brownout) hazard.
  • Also unused: PIN_BAT_CHG_EN (39) and PIN_EXTERNAL_POWER (9) — the firmware can't even tell it's on USB power, which is exactly the signal that should gate "always-on relay mode" vs "sleepy battery mode".

docs.title: P1-1 · Data race on the ask path: two tasks share static buffers with no lock
docs.text: • tiny_node_do_ask() uses static char audio_url[256] and static char ask_resp[8192] (tiny_node.cpp:140,157). It is called from both the node loop (relay ask/voice envelopes, dispatch at tiny_node.cpp:223) and voice_ask_task (AI button, tiny_button.cpp:29). A button press during a relay-driven ask (an 80 s window! timeout at tiny_node.cpp:158) corrupts both requests. Needs a mutex or single-owner queue (the depth-1 s_ask_q protects only button-vs-button).

docs.title: P1-2 · One blocking loop = heartbeat starvation
docs.text: • node_task is a single sequential loop; a dispatch that runs an 80 s ask, a 15 s record, or an OTA download stalls heartbeats (30 s cadence, tiny_node.cpp:326) and relay polls → backend sees the device offline exactly while it's busiest. Heartbeat cadence is also wrong in practice: 6 × (5 s delay + HTTP time) ≈ 40-60 s, not 30 s.

docs.title: P1-3 · Every HTTP call is a fresh TLS handshake
docs.text: • http_json_t does esp_http_client_init … cleanup per call (tiny_node.cpp:60-81): relay poll every 5 s = a full TLS handshake every 5 s. This is the single biggest battery line-item (see below) and adds 1-2 s latency to every envelope. Use one persistent client / keep-alive connection.

docs.title: P1-4 · AI button semantics diverge from spec, and 8 KB stack is thin for the TLS ask path
docs.text:
• Spec (official stock UX + roadmap): hold AI = voice input, single click = home/wake. Implemented: single click fires a 6 s voice ask immediately (tiny_button.cpp:36-40); no long-press callback at all; Up/Down only post device_note events. There is no local "cancel recording" either — once clicked, the mic records 6 s no matter what.
  • voice_ask_task gets 8192 B (tiny_button.cpp:66) and runs record → media upload (TLS) → 80 s ask (TLS) → tiny_display_render_card. mbedTLS + cJSON + renderer nested in one 8 KB task is close to the edge; measure uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark and bump to 12 K, or route the button through the node task instead of a parallel TLS client (also fixes P1-1).

docs.title: P1-5 · Boot uses ESP_ERROR_CHECK on non-essential peripherals → panic-reboot loop
docs.text: • tiny_main.cpp:57-59: a transient failure in tiny_display_init() or sticky_buzzer_init() aborts → reboot → re-latch power → abort … forever, with no way for the user to power off (the latch is held before the check). Display is arguably essential; the buzzer is not. Degrade gracefully: log + render an error state where possible, and only hard-fail on board_init().

docs.title: P2 — polish / correctness notes
docs.text:
• Task WDT: enabled, 5 s, idle-task watch only (sdkconfig:1186-1191) — fine. No task subscribes explicitly; node_task's longest in-iteration blocking call is bounded (HTTP timeout 15 s / 80 s) and it never starves idle thanks to vTaskDelays. No interrupt WDT concerns seen. OK, but consider esp_task_wdt_add for tiny_node with a generous timeout so a wedged TLS stack reboots instead of hanging forever.
  • Serial card console loop (tiny_main.cpp:100-135): correct VFS/driver hookup, overflow drops the line silently (pos = 0, tiny_main.cpp:133) — prints nothing; emit CARD_RESULT overflow so the bench harness isn't left guessing. Config path does naive strchr for the inner { — a "config" value containing { inside a string would misparse; acceptable for a bench tool.
  • board.cpp wake path (board.cpp:34-47): re-drives HOLD/LOCK before gpio_deep_sleep_hold_dis() — correct order, good. PIN_POWER_LOCK is held HIGH permanently; stock semantics pulse it — verify against Seeed demo before the first battery-only power cycle test.
  • SD: PIN_SD_EN driven 1 at boot (board.cpp:96) with the comment "powered off" — verify polarity of the load switch; if EN=1 means ON, the SD rail idles powered for nothing (a few mA). Same check for PIN_TOUCH_EN/PIN_EPD_EN polarities in the sleep path.
  • Buzzer (sticky_buzzer.cpp): 2.4 kHz, duty 256/1024 (25 %), 60 ms — audible but quiet; for a passive buzzer max loudness is 50 % duty. sticky_buzzer_beep blocks its caller 60 ms (called from touch/button paths — fine). Only ONE chime exists; tiny_audio_chime(name) ignores its argument (tiny_audio.cpp:109), so "ask"/"ack"/"error" are indistinguishable to the user — cheap win: 3 distinct pitch patterns.
  • PDM capture (tiny_audio.cpp): pins/clk/slot config correct per official docs (CLK 19, DATA 20, mono 16 k s16); rail clean-cycle (150 ms off) present per recording — good. WAV header correct. Buffer in PSRAM — good. Full channel create/delete per recording is wasteful but safe. goto fail before i2s_channel_enable succeeded calls i2s_channel_disable on a non-enabled channel — returns an error, harmless, but check err. No gain/AGC — PDM raw may be quiet; worth a 4-6 dB software gain pass before upload.
  • Battery driver: reads only SoC; BQ27220 also gives voltage/current/temp — add to status and heartbeat body for fleet telemetry. No design-capacity programming (BQ27220 defaults may misreport SoC until configured for 750 mAh).
  • hb_countdown decrements after poll_relay even when Wi-Fi bounce continues earlier — cadence drift only, harmless.

docs.title: Battery-life estimate (750 mAh, current firmware behavior)
docs.text:
Model: Wi-Fi STA always connected, IDF default WIFI_PS_MIN_MODEM (no explicit esp_wifi_set_ps call found — default modem-sleep applies), relay poll every 5 s with a fresh TLS handshake each time (P1-3), heartbeat ~every 40 s.

State Current (typ, S3 + radio) Duty TLS handshake + HTTPS round-trip ~120-150 mA ~1.5-2.5 s per 5 s cycle (~35 %) Connected idle, modem-sleep (DTIM) ~15-25 mA ~65 % E-ink refresh ~25 mA for 1-2 s negligible amortized

Average ≈ 0.35·135 + 0.65·20 ≈ ~60 mA → 750 mAh / 60 mA ≈ 12 h (call it 9-14 h depending on RSSI and backend latency). Matches the "dies overnight" failure mode.

What each fix buys: 1. Keep-alive TLS connection (P1-3): poll shrinks to ~0.2-0.3 s of radio → avg ≈ 27 mA → ~27 h. Biggest single win, pure software. 2. Adaptive polling (5 s only for ~2 min after interaction/envelope, else 30-60 s) + keep-alive: avg ≈ 12-15 mA → ~2-2.5 days. 3. Light sleep between polls (esp_pm + auto light-sleep, Wi-Fi beacon-only): avg ≈ 5-8 mA → ~4-6 days. 4. Scheduled deep sleep (wake on GPIO4 or timer every N min for a mailbox check; e-ink retains the last card for free): idle floor ~0.1-0.3 mA (latch + gauge) → weeks, at the cost of relay latency. None of 2-4 exists today; esp_pm isn't configured and no esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_MAX_MODEM) option is exposed. Recommend: USB-powered ⇒ current always-on behavior; battery ⇒ tier 2 minimum, tier 4 below 20 % SoC — gated on PIN_EXTERNAL_POWER (GPIO9), which is currently unread (P0-3).

docs.title: Boot-order review (for the record)
docs.text: app_main (tiny_main.cpp:55-99): log wake cause → board_init (latch first — correct and documented as a contract) → display → buzzer → splash+beep → 8 s photo delay → demo card → touch → audio → battery → buttons → config→wifi→node → serial console loop. Order is sound; failure handling is the issue (P1-5), and tiny_boot_early() should be the true first line once it exists (P0-1) — the USB-JTAG demux must run before any I2S/mic init after a deep-sleep wake.

docs.title: Touch + Input Layer Audit — 2026-08-25 (auditor 1, full read)
P0-1: The stale-region bug — unsynchronized region publication + regions published at draw time, not display time, with three unserialized render callers
docs.text:
The race, exactly:

  1. s_regions/s_region_count are plain statics with zero synchronization (tiny_display.cpp:82-83). Writer: draw_buttons() (tiny_display.cpp:85-109) runs on whichever task called tiny_display_render_card. Reader: tiny_display_button_regions() (tiny_display.cpp:111-115) runs on tiny_touch task (prio 5, 30ms poll). There are three concurrent render callers: the tiny_node task (tiny_node.cpp:168,178,198), the voice_ask task (via tiny_node_do_ask, tiny_button.cpp:27), and the main task serial card console (tiny_main.cpp:125). None hold a lock; the shared Canvas isn't locked either. A tap landing while draw_buttons is mid-write reads a torn s_regions[i] — struct assigned with label={0} at tiny_display.cpp:104 before strlcpy fills it at :105. A zeroed label printed through printf("label=\"%s\"") is empty/garbage → the observed label=?.

  2. Regions are committed ~2 seconds before the panel shows the card. draw_buttons updates s_regions during canvas draw (tiny_display.cpp:198), but the user still sees the old card until sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() (tiny_display.cpp:217, full refresh, 1–2s) completes. Any tap in that window hit-tests the invisible new layout. Conversely, a finger already down on the old card resolves at lift (on_tap_up, tiny_touch.cpp:62) against whatever regions exist at lift time → the observed tap-resolved-against-the-previous-card. The tiny_touch.h:2 region struct even has a card_id field designed for this — and tiny_touch_set_regions is an empty stub (tiny_touch.cpp:149-152), so card identity is never checked.

The atomic fix (three parts, all small):

// tiny_display.cpp
static portMUX_TYPE s_region_mux = portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED;
static uint32_t s_card_gen = 0;   // bumped once per COMMITTED card

// in render_card: build regions into a LOCAL array during draw_buttons;
// publish only AFTER refresh returns ESP_OK:
esp_err_t err = sticky_display_refresh_monochrome();
if (err == ESP_OK) {
    taskENTER_CRITICAL(&s_region_mux);
    memcpy(s_regions, local_regions, sizeof s_regions);
    s_region_count = local_count;
    ++s_card_gen;
    taskEXIT_CRITICAL(&s_region_mux);
}

// reader returns gen: int tiny_display_button_regions(out, max, uint32_t *gen)

In tiny_touch.cpp: snapshot gen at finger-down (touch_task where s_touching flips true, :99), re-read at lift in on_tap_up; if gen changed mid-press, drop the tap (the ground moved under the finger — iOS does the same when a view disappears under a touch). Additionally serialize the three render callers with one SemaphoreHandle_t display mutex around the whole render_card body (canvas + panel are also unprotected — concurrent serial-console + relay renders currently corrupt the framebuffer, a second latent P0 hiding behind the same lock).

docs.title: P0-2: No tap feedback is wired — and the parts all exist
docs.text:
on_tap_up (tiny_touch.cpp:62-86) prints a serial line and queues a device_note — no buzzer, no visual ack. Yet: - sticky_buzzer_beep() exists and works (sticky_buzzer.cpp:51, used at boot tiny_main.cpp:61), - tiny_audio_chime() exists and is wired for the physical AI button path (tiny_node.cpp:143,146) — but not for screen taps, - sticky_display_refresh_partial() exists in the vendored HAL (sticky_display.h:23) and is used by nothing; tiny_display_blit_1bit explicitly discards its partial flag (tiny_display.cpp:242).

This is precisely why the user reported "touch doesn't work" while 12/12 taps were actually delivered. Fix: in on_tap_up, on a button hit: (a) sticky_buzzer_beep() immediately (<1ms, works from any task); (b) invert the button rect on the canvas and push it via sticky_display_refresh_partial() (~300-500ms, region-sized). Perceived latency drops from "nothing happened" to ~instant audio + sub-second visual. This must run before the network device_note round-trip, never after. Do NOT run the partial refresh on the touch task itself (e-ink busy-wait up to 10s, sticky_display.cpp:123) — queue it to the render owner.

docs.title: P1-1: Fast taps (<~60ms contact) are silently dropped
docs.text: kDebouncePolls = 2 at 30ms poll (tiny_touch.cpp:26,38) means a contact must span ≥2 polls; a crisp tap can be 40–60ms. The ghost-touch defence throws away real input. Better discriminator: GT911 reports contact area — GTPoint.size (gt911.h:21) is already read and ignored by touch_task (tiny_touch.cpp:92). Phantom points characteristically report size == 0. Accept single-poll contacts with size > 0; keep the streak rule only for size-0 points. Also: the GT911 INT pin is wired (PIN_TOUCH_INT, tiny_touch.cpp:134) but the driver reset leaves it as OUTPUT (gt911.cpp:71); INT-driven wakeup = lower latency + zero idle I2C traffic.

docs.title: P1-2: Hit-test uses the lift-off point, not the touch-down point
docs.text: on_tap_up tests s_last_x/s_last_y (tiny_touch.cpp:71-72). Fingers roll on lift; iOS hit-tests the touch-down location and only requires lift within slop. Fix: hit-test s_start_x/s_start_y; capture provisional coords on poll 1 (today s_start isn't captured until the debounce streak completes, tiny_touch.cpp:99).

docs.title: P1-3: 5-second boot grace swallows taps with no user signal
docs.text: kBootGraceMs = 5000 (tiny_touch.cpp:39,93-96) hard-drops every touch after init while the panel shows tappable buttons. Shorten to the observed ghost window, or use the size>0 filter from P1-1 and delete the grace entirely.

docs.title: P1-4: tiny_display_button_regions return-value contract is a footgun
docs.text: Fills min(count,max) entries but returns s_region_count unclamped (tiny_display.cpp:112-114). Any future caller iterating the return over a smaller buffer reads uninitialized stack.

docs.title: P2 — robustness / polish
docs.text:
• Multi-touch truncated, not modeled — read_points(&p, 1) (tiny_touch.cpp:92); future pinch/two-finger needs maxPoints=2+ + per-id tracking (driver already returns id).
  • GT911 large-area flag (0x40) ignored — palm rejection is free by checking it.
  • vTaskDelayUntil catch-up burst (tiny_touch.cpp:110) — reset next after long stalls.
  • Starvation: touch never blocks on network (tiny_node_post_event queue-send timeout 0, tiny_node.cpp:356-363 — correctly designed). Landmine: any direct refresh call on the touch task can stall it seconds. Bump touch to prio 6 (above node) and keep it I/O-free.
  • Physical buttons (tiny_button.cpp): solid structure; missing chime on UP/DOWN click; BUTTON_LONG_PRESS configured (2000ms, :50) but never registered — AI-button long-press is dead.
  • tiny_touch_set_regions stub (tiny_touch.cpp:149) is the right long-term home for the fix — cards carrying card_id + button ids mean taps report semantic ids, not indices.

docs.title: Gesture roadmap (e-ink-appropriate)
docs.text:
The state machine already computes everything needed: s_start_*, s_last_*, streak (≈duration); the slop check at tiny_touch.cpp:65 already detects swipes — it just discards them.

Gesture Detection E-ink verb Tap today's path + P0/P1 fixes button activate Swipe L/R adx > 80 && adx > 2*ady at lift page/card history nav (stock UX parity; synonym of UP/DOWN keys) Swipe from left edge s_start_x < 30 + right swipe back/dismiss card Swipe up from bottom s_start_y > 450 + up home card Long-press streak ≥ ~25 polls (750ms), < slop movement — fire AT threshold with buzzer blip context menu (pin / screenshot / ask-about-this) Drag do NOT build — e-ink can't animate tracking — Double-tap do NOT build — panel can't ack fast enough to make the rhythm learnable —

Ordering: P0-1 + P0-2 together (two halves of the live bug report), then P1-1/P1-2, then swipes (~20 lines once tap machine is trustworthy), long-press last.

docs.title: Pocket bumper case
docs.text:
Provenance

This page is case/README.md included verbatim — the case lane's own documentation, written next to the .scad source it describes (commit 078dec6). The preview renders are copied alongside; the printable sticky_case.stl / .3mf and the parametric sticky_case.scad live in the repo's case/ directory. The design answers the pocket-carry directive: glass never touches pocket contents, magnets keep working, and — the part worth copying — nothing is cut where nothing was measured.

docs.title: Sticky pocket bumper case
docs.text: Corner-bumper case for the Seeed reTerminal Sticky — pocket-first protection per the design directive: the glass never touches pocket contents, the four N52 corner magnets keep working, and nothing is cut where we could not measure.

docs.title: Design decision — why a corner bumper, not a full shell
docs.text:
There is no authoritative mechanical source for the Sticky's edge layout:

  • Seeed-Projects/OSHW-reTerminal-Sticky — 404 (checked 2026-08-26)
  • GitHub code search for a vendor STEP — no hits
  • seeedstudio.com/sticky/docs hardware-overview — dimensions + internals only, no drawing, no button/USB positions

The buttons (AI/Power, Up, Down), the USB-C recovery port, the PDM mic hole and the buzzer port all live on the device's edges at positions we cannot verify. House rule: an unverified cutout is a wrong cutout. So all four edge middles are fully open — every edge feature stays reachable no matter where it actually is, USB-C recovery flashing works in-case, mic and buzzer are never sealed. Only the four corners are wrapped.

The front face is completely unobstructed except a 0.8 mm retention lip at the corners — swipe-from-edge gestures survive because the lip exists only over the corner radii, never along the straight edges.

docs.text: parameter value basis device body 106.0 × 65.5 × 7.3 mm MEASURED (vendor spec, docs/hardware.md) clearance per side 0.30 mm brief (0.25–0.3) cavity 106.6 × 66.1 mm derived outer envelope 110.6 × 70.1 × 9.3 mm (+ lanyard ear) derived wall thickness 2.0 mm brief ≥1.6, upsized for pocket duty back rim 6.0 mm wide × 1.0 mm thick magnet compromise, see below lip above glass 1.0 mm brief lip inward overhang 0.8 mm (corners only) retention vs. gesture tradeoff corner wrap length 26 mm from each corner leaves ≥45 mm open per edge middle outer corner radius 5.0 mm pocket-friendly lanyard hole ⌀3.0 mm, bottom-left ear optional cord

docs.title: Measured vs. assumed ledger (bench discipline)
docs.text: item status detail body W×H×T MEASURED vendor spec 106 × 65.5 × 7.3, confirmed in our docs body corner radius ASSUMED = 4.0 mm eyeballed from product photos; if the real radius differs the corner fit changes — caliper it and adjust body_corner_r button / USB / mic / buzzer edge positions UNKNOWN — designed around no STEP, no drawing; all edge middles left open so no cutout can be wrong magnet positions ASSUMED corner zones "N52 in all four corners" is spec; exact XY unknown, so the entire back is ≤1 mm or open glass plane flush with body top ASSUMED photos show near-flush glass; lip height is measured from body top

docs.title: Magnet tradeoff (stated, per brief)
docs.text: The back is skeletal: a 6 mm-wide, 1.0 mm-thick rim plus fully open center. N52 magnets pull usefully through 1 mm of PLA — expect roughly 30–50 % holding-force loss vs. bare metal contact. If wall-mount grip matters more than back protection, print with back_rim_w smaller or drop back_t to 0.6 (2–3 layers); if pocket protection matters more, this is the right default. The corners themselves are where the magnets sit, and the rim covers them with exactly the 1 mm ceiling the brief allows.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Snap-in, no screws: tilt one long edge under the corner lips, press the opposite corners down — the 0.8 mm lips flex over the body and capture the glass perimeter at four points. Removal: push a thumb through the open back.

docs.title: Validation (strands-cad, 2026-08-26)
docs.text:
check result watertight ✅ trimesh.is_watertight = True, single solid volume 5.996 cm³ (stl_volume) mass 7.44 g PLA / 7.62 g PETG @ 100 % infill (stl_weight) printability (stl_printability, X1C) fits bed ✅ · 0 % overhang area · bed contact 2653 mm² · supports: no inertia (sim_inertia_from_stl) COM ≈ (−0.5, −0.3, 3.1) mm — essentially centered

Honesty note: the brief's sanity band was ~10–25 g; a skeletal corner bumper is simply lighter than that. Chasing the band would mean thickening the back over the magnets or closing the edges — both worse designs. 7.4 g is the honest mass of the right shape.

docs.title: Print settings (suggested)
docs.text:
• Orientation: back face down, exactly as the STL sits — flat, no supports
  • Material: PETG preferred (lip flexes repeatedly; PLA works, snap gently)
  • Layer: 0.16–0.20 mm · Walls: 3 · Infill: irrelevant (part is nearly all wall)
  • No brim needed (2653 mm² bed contact); no supports (0 % overhang — the lip's underside is a 45° chamfer by construction)
