docs.title: Dashboard — sticky.cagatay.my
docs.text:
A remote-control cockpit for the Sticky: device status, live screen mirror, a render_ui composer, action buttons and an activity feed — served behind a WebAuthn passkey gate at https://sticky.cagatay.my (Cloudflare Tunnel sticky, backend on localhost:8787).

Code lives in docs/dashboard/: FastAPI backend (server.py) + React/Vite SPA (frontend/), launched by run.sh.

docs.title: How it controls the device
docs.text:
The Sticky is not on a LAN socket — it's controlled through the tiny.technology device relay:

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser (passkey)
    participant D as Dashboard backend
    participant T as tiny.technology
    participant S as Sticky
    B->>D: POST /api/invoke {command}
    D->>T: POST /api/devices/relay {toDevice, payload:{type:"invoke",prompt}}
    T-->>D: {id: "env_…"}
    S->>T: PUT /api/devices/relay (5s poll)
    T-->>S: envelope
    S->>T: PATCH /api/devices/relay (reply)
    D->>T: GET /api/devices/relay?inReplyTo=env_…
    T-->>D: reply {result, images?}
    D-->>B: result

Two credentials, two directions:

  • the backend authenticates to tiny.technology as the owner — the same Bearer credential the tiny CLI writes to ~/.tiny/credentials.json (override: TINY_CREDENTIALS)
  • the browser authenticates to the backend with a passkey — WebAuthn (Touch ID / Face ID); the private key never leaves the secure enclave, the backend stores only the public key (.sticky_auth.json, chmod 600)

The async contract mirrors use_device: an invoke waits up to 45 s, then returns {pending, envelope_id}; GET /api/result/{envelope_id} redeems the reply later (the relay mailbox keeps it ~24 h). Image URLs in replies pass the same plugin.tiny.technology/media/* allowlist the tiny agents apply.

docs.title: Live mode — the real fridge panel
docs.text:
STICKY_MOCK=0 STICKY_DEVICE=sticky ./run.sh          # what runs today

Live mode is the production mode. The rules it plays by (fw 0.14.18-m12) — every one of them exists because the first live attempt lied on screen:

thing how live mode handles it status reply shape since 0.9.x the firmware answers machine-readable JSON (fw, battery_pct, charging, wifi, ssid, rssi_dbm, heap_free, psram_free, + a human summary field). parse_status() still accepts the older English sentence and reports which shape it saw; absent fields render as —, never as a guess. GET /api/status is the normalized route. screen mirror the screenshot verb uploads the framebuffer and answers with a hosted URL in the reply text (screenshot: https://plugin.tiny.technology/media/…png), not in images[]. The backend extracts it, checks it against is_device_media_url, and proxies the bytes at the guarded /api/screen.png — so the mirror is the REAL panel and the media URL never has to be exposed to the browser. clickable mirror the relay cannot read the panel's current card back, so the backend remembers the last card spec it sent and derives button boxes with the firmware's own geometry (800×480, margin 24, 56 px bar at the bottom, gap 16, n≤4 split evenly — pixel-verified against a device screenshot). clicking a button a click cannot press the glass. It is logged as sim_tap and labelled "simulated" in the feed and in the UI. Real taps come from the device: the firmware posts them as device_note ui_tap button=N label=…, and the backend reads them owner-side from GET /api/events, showing them as ui_tap (source device). Tap zones whose id/label the firmware itself will act on (the action_for() sniff — m: rows, rescan wifi, …) are badged ⚡ with a dashed outline, and the tooltip says exactly what a real finger would also trigger; report-only zones stay clean. The badge runs the same deviceActionFor mirror as the composer lint — one truth, two surfaces. verbs the firmware lacks wake, reprovision, image, stream are refused with HTTP 501 + the reason, and their Action buttons are greyed out with that reason. An action that does nothing is a lie on the screen. slow envelopes every relay call runs in a threadpool (run_in_threadpool), so a 60 s pending invoke never freezes the dashboard — and a pending envelope is tracked, not dropped — and since the reaper went autonomous, redemption no longer depends on a browser being open: the registry persists to disk on every mutation (a launchd respawn mid-deploy no longer orphans in-flight envelopes), and a startup task polls every 20 s only while envelopes are in flight, blanket-caught so the reaper never dies. A late reply still lands in the feed (marked ↩), a late render_ui still updates the mirror's card truth, a late screenshot still updates the mirror image. After 15 min unanswered it's logged as expired (⌛) — abandoned visibly, never silently. In-flight envelopes are surfaced in /api/activity and as a banner. The original design redeemed only on activity polls — which meant owner out, late replies rot; that gap was found by its own fixtures (chart envelopes orphaned by a respawn) and closed.

Verbs that actually exist (fw 0.14.18-m12): render_ui <card-json>, status, sensors [card], say <text>, ask <text>, voice [secs], screenshot, miccheck [secs], page <nav>, rotate [deg|auto], tap <x> <y>, scroll [up|down|top|±px], sleep [secs], ota [channel], messages [unread|thread <login>] — the verb-by-verb reference is Commands.

Since the capabilities pass, verb truth comes from the device itself: /api/capabilities crosses the dashboard's static table with the verbs the firmware advertises in its own heartbeat (verified live: 15 verbs round-trip). A verb shipped by OTA lights its button without a dashboard deploy — the Sensors button staying grey for a day was exactly this staleness class. The semantics are honest in both directions: the device's word wins; unadvertised verbs grey out with the reason; verbs the firmware advertises that have no dedicated UI yet get a 🆕 chip pointing at the raw console; and if the platform is unreachable the static table takes over with the footer naming which source is speaking.

The verb console covers all of them with structured controls, not a free-text box: a nav ring for page (home/status/sensors/settings/wifi/ble + back/prev/next), a rotation control (0/90/180/270/auto/report, with the device's IMU answer read back), miccheck with a live/SILENT verdict badge parsed from the JSON reply, and sleep with timer-wake seconds. The console builds positional prompts for every sscanf-parsed verb — a lesson paid for on real glass: the first say implementation sent JSON and the panel dutifully rendered the literal braces. The screen mirror carries scroll controls (⤒ ▲ ▼) that drive the glass's own scroll verb and read back its pixel receipts (offset/content_h), refreshing the mirror after each step — scrolling the real panel from the browser, with the panel's own numbers as proof.

docs.title: Mock mode — the software Sticky
docs.text: STICKY_MOCK=1 (the default) swaps the relay for mock_device.py, which implements the device end of the envelope contract per the API contract — envelope dispatch, sleep-gating, help-on-unknown — and renders card specs to a real 800×480 PNG quantized to the 4 e-ink gray levels. It implements every verb, including the ones the firmware has not shipped, so it is the right target for UI work; a mock click is a real ui_tap because the mock device is the one being clicked.

docs.title: Auth lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Unclaimed: /auth/status → setup_required. First enrollment is gated by STICKY_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN (the UI asks for it) so a public URL never has an open enrollment window — without the token, register/begin answers 403.
  2. Sealed: every /api/* route requires the session JWT (cookie or Authorization: Bearer); unauthenticated → 401. Additional passkeys can be added from a signed-in session; the last passkey cannot be deleted.
  3. Sessions last 24 h (STICKY_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL). A mid-session expiry is handled as one event: the first 401 on /api with a held token raises a single banner and the login gate — not a wall of failing cards.

Verified end-to-end with a CDP virtual authenticator (puppeteer + system Chrome): register → seal → invoke → clickable mirror tap → logout → passkey login, plus cookie-less 401/403 checks against the public URL.

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
card source 📟 Device status — fw/battery/wifi/heap/display GET /api/status (both reply shapes), 30 s 🛰 Fleet row — name/id/kind/online/last seen GET /api/device → platform /api/devices, 60 s 🪞 Screen mirror — the real frame, clickable POST /api/screenshot → /api/screen.png + /api/buttons 🎨 render_ui composer — presets + JSON editor + live lint render_ui envelope (card spec v1) — the lint mirrors the firmware dispatch (7 types, keys, buttons≤4, priority), warns without blocking (the glass's receipt is the judge; only JSON parse errors block); presets include a scrollable 24-row list and an alert card. The lint is pinned to a declared grammar (LINT_GRAMMAR=2, stated next to the rules it mirrors), and status polls feed fwGrammar — the device is the only authority on what it speaks. On mismatch the Status card raises a ⚠ drift banner and every lint result confesses which version its rules mirror. The design proved itself the same night it shipped: grammar v2 (the messages dialect) reached the glass within hours of the pin landing, the banner fired unprompted on the first 0.14.11 poll, and the lint was then caught up — v2's real definition (verbs + button-id namespaces like m:, not card types) with the m: rows annotated. The Status row also shows fw_commit, so the panel can prove the deploy's ancestry at a glance ⚡ Actions — ask, voice ask, OTA (+greyed-out gaps) GET /api/capabilities decides what is clickable. The ota action carries a direction guard: a fresh status probe captures fw_before, the reply returns ota_guard{fw_before,note}, and staging opens a 30-minute watch: every parsed status receipt feeds the redeem, which logs the verdict itself — ⬆✅ upgraded, ⬆🚨 DOWNGRADED, ⌛ expired-unredeemed — receipts-based, because the channel pointer is device-token-auth'd and direction is provable only by evidence, not intent 💬 Messages — owner inbox, threads, unread badge, compose GET /api/messages (owner-side poll, 60 s); opening a thread (GET /api/messages/{peer}) is the explicit act that marks it read — and logs itself to the activity feed as dm_open, because a read-marking side effect should leave a trace. Sending is real: POST /api/messages delivers a DM through the owner relay (send_dm) — body capped at 2000 code points and rejected over-length, never truncated; an empty message is refused; the reply reports actual delivery (telegram/push/stored). Every send carries viaTiny provenance: a message composed by an agent or this dashboard must never claim a human typed it. 📟 deep-link buttons push the firmware's messages / messages thread <login> verbs — the same inbox or conversation appears on the physical glass, fetched by the device with its own token 📜 Activity — envelopes, replies, REAL ui_taps, sim_taps /api/activity ring + platform event ring, 5 s poll — entries render in receipt language (↕ scroll offsets in px, 🎨 committed-to-glass, ↩ late reply, ⌛ expired, ⏳ pending), and a ⬇ export button hands the whole session (receipts + in-flight) to another lane as timestamped JSON

The Sensors card exists now — but as an on-demand read, never a poll (each real read power-cycles the gyro, and a 30 s poll would spend the 750 mAh pack to decorate a dashboard). /api/sensors passes the firmware's JSON through verbatim — field names measured off tiny_sensors.cpp's emitters, not predicted — and the render is provenance-honest: gyro renders live dps when the read carries values (measured: it does), and a null gyro is explained as powered-down rather than dressed up as an error, absolute mAh appears only when mah_trusted is true, and an untrusted gauge is explained with its own numbers (design 7500 vs pack 750) rather than hidden. The card shows what the device knows and how much the device trusts what it knows.

docs.title: The HTTP surface
docs.text:
Every route in server.py, so integrators never have to read the cards table sideways. All /api/* routes require the session JWT (cookie or Bearer) except /api/health; /auth/* is the WebAuthn lifecycle.

route what it does GET /api/health unauthenticated liveness: mode (mock/live), device selector, whether first-passkey setup is still required GET /api/capabilities the device's own advertised verb list — what the UI is allowed to light up GET /api/device fleet row for the selected device via platform /api/devices POST /api/invoke raw verb → relay envelope; waits ≤ 45 s then returns {pending, envelope_id} (the use_device contract) GET /api/result/{envelope_id} redeem a pending envelope later (relay mailbox keeps ~24 h) GET /api/status · GET /api/sensors normalized status (both reply shapes) · firmware sensor JSON passed through verbatim POST /api/screenshot → GET /api/screen.png trigger a framebuffer upload, then proxy the allowlisted media URL — the browser never sees it GET /api/buttons the tap zones of the last card, with bboxes, for the clickable mirror POST /api/tap simulated only, and it says so: refuses ids not on the last card sent from here (404), logs sim_tap with "the device did NOT feel this". Real ui_taps arrive the other way — device → platform event ring → activity feed GET /api/messages · GET /api/messages/{peer} · POST /api/messages inbox · thread (marks read, logs dm_open) · real DM send with the viaTiny provenance flag (see the Messages card row) GET /api/activity receipt-language feed + in_flight envelopes + upstream events_error when the platform pull is failing GET /auth/status · POST /auth/register/begin·finish · POST /auth/login/begin·finish · POST /auth/logout · GET·DELETE /auth/credentials passkey lifecycle — first enrollment gated by STICKY_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN; the last passkey cannot be deleted GET /{path} the built PWA (SPA fallback)

docs.title: Concrete findings (iter 1 research — verified against source)
Owner-side wire surface (~/tinyai-id)
docs.text:
The Sticky is driven via relay envelopes; the owner side is session-authenticated:

verb route body/query returns send envelope POST https://tiny.technology/api/devices/relay {toDevice: "<deviceId>", payload: {type:"invoke", prompt:"<cmd> <json>"}} (payload may be object or string; route stringifies) {ok:true, id:"env_…"} — statuses: 404 no_such_device, 413 too_big, 400 bad, 424 relay-side poll reply GET /api/devices/relay?inReplyTo=env_… session {ok, reply?} — reply payload is a serialized JSON string {"result":…,"images":[{url,format}]} list devices GET /api/devices session {ok, devices:[{id,name,last_seen,capabilities,…}]}

Device-side verbs (PUT poll / PATCH reply) are device-token-in-body — that's what the mock simulates.

docs.text: ~/.tiny/credentials.json = {version, apiUrl, token(JWT Bearer), user{id,login,…}, expires} — the exact credential tiny-tech CLI uses (api.ts:55 sends Authorization: Bearer <token>). The dashboard backend reads this file directly (env TINY_CREDENTIALS overrides path). Expires 2026-11 — no action needed from cagatay now; on 401 the backend surfaces "re-login with npx tiny-tech" in the UI. ~/.tiny/device.json holds this Mac's device token (tind_…) — NOT used by the dashboard.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
From a boxed reTerminal Sticky to a device on your tiny fleet, in four steps.

Before anything: secure your way back

Read Recovery first. Step zero on a fresh unit is a full 32 MB flash dump — that dump is your unit-specific restore (NVS, serial, calibration included). The official factory image is the fallback. The ESP32-S3 ROM bootloader survives any bad app flash; the device is unbrickable in practice, but only if you kept a way back to stock.

docs.title: 0. Back up stock firmware (once, ~45 min)
docs.text:
# NOTE: high baud rates fail through USB hub chains ("serial noise") — 115200 is reliable
~/.tiny/pypi/bin/esptool --port /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881 read-flash 0 0x2000000 stock-firmware-32MB.bin
shasum -a 256 stock-firmware-32MB.bin > stock-firmware-32MB.bin.sha256

docs.title: 1. Build + flash the tiny firmware
docs.text:
Requires ESP-IDF v5.4 (the version Seeed's demos are built and tested on).

cd firmware
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py build
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881 flash monitor

The partition plan keeps a factory slot with the last-known-good build; OTA updates go to ota_0/ota_1 with trial-boot + rollback, and USB flashing is always available regardless of what OTA did.

docs.title: 2. Provision Wi-Fi (the tiny-XXXX portal)
docs.text:
On first boot — or after a revoked token trips the 3-strike auth-halt, which reopens the portal by itself (there is no reprovision verb to call; see not-verbs) — the e-ink shows a setup card with a QR code:

  1. Join the access point tiny-XXXX (password tinysetup) — or scan the QR, which encodes exactly that
  2. The portal lives at 192.168.4.1:
  3. GET /info → {"kind":"reterminal-sticky", "name":…, "mac":…, "provisioned":false}
  4. POST /setup with {device_id, token, api?, name?, networks:[{ssid,key},…]}
  5. GET / serves a minimal HTML form as the manual fallback
  6. The device saves config to NVS and reboots onto your Wi-Fi

The portal is byte-compatible with the Nicla necklaces, so the tiny iOS app's "add device" flow onboards the Sticky unchanged — it joins the AP, posts the credentials it minted at enrollment, done.

docs.title: 3. Enroll on tiny.technology
docs.text:
Enrollment (POST /api/devices) happens on the app side — the iOS app (or CLI) creates the device row and mints the tind_… device token that the portal then hands to the device. After reboot the Sticky:

  • heartbeats every 30 s (POST /api/devices/heartbeat) advertising its capabilities
  • polls for envelopes every 5 s (PUT /api/devices/relay)

docs.title: 4. Talk to it
docs.text:
From any tiny surface:

use_device invoke → prompt: "render_ui {\"type\":\"text\",\"title\":\"Dinner\",\"body\":\"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge\"}"
use_device invoke → prompt: "screenshot"
use_device invoke → prompt: "status"

Or press the AI button on the device itself and ask tiny a question by voice — long-press is the home key.

The full command surface (render_ui · say · screenshot · page · rotate · tap · swipe · scroll · status · sensors · miccheck · ask · voice · messages · sleep · ota) is documented verb-by-verb in Commands, the card spec in Cards, and the exact wire shapes in the API contract. For browser-based control, see the Dashboard.

Something misbehaving — silent cards, ghost taps, a 422 on voice? The Troubleshooting field guide covers every defect we've actually seen on this hardware, with the shipped fix.
